stories.title: Have Brahmin MPs tied ghungroos? asks Alankar Agnihotri:Bareilly city magistrate calls situation like civil war, warns generations will blame today’s silence
stories.summary: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, a PCS officer from the Brahmin community, resigned on Monday, expressing anger over what he described as an insult to Shankaracharya and the new UGC law. Agnihotri questioned, “Do you want the genocide of Brahmins? I want to ask Brahmin MPs and MLAs, will you remain silent even when sisters and daughters are raped on the streets? What bells have you worn, and when will you speak? Who was the Prayagraj DM cooking bread for? Is he a Shankaracharya?” He cited both the UGC’s new law and the assault on disciples of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand as key reasons for his resignation. Dainik Bhaskar conducted a special interview with him following the announcement. Read the full conversation... Question: Why did you suddenly resign? Answer: For some time now, the situations that have developed in the state are going from bad to worse. A campaign is being run against a particular class, especially Brahmins, which has now become unbearable. Sometimes, bulldozers run over someone's house, and sometimes people are beaten to death in police stations. In jail, a deputy jailer killed a disabled person and another Brahmin. The most tragic incident is from the Prayagraj Magh Mela. The disciples of Avimukteshwaranand Maharaj were grabbed by their tuft (shikha) and beaten up. Such videos have emerged that make one's soul tremble. When administration officials themselves treat revered saints and their disciples this way, what message will it send to society? Is this preparation for the genocide of Brahmins? What do they want to achieve? Question: Are you questioning the current system? Answer: You say that he is not Shankaracharya at all. What do you want to say? Are those who are roaming around in big cars Shankaracharya? You are giving them VIP treatment. Your officials are taking photos with them. Your officials are warming up with them. Which Shankaracharya are they? Why is the administration doing so much flattery? The DM of Prayagraj is warming up with them. What authority does he have to warm up there? Nothing happened to them. On one hand, the disciples of the real Shankaracharya are being beaten, on the other hand, top administrative officials are sitting with some so-called saints, warming up and getting photos taken. Has the administration now become a hub of sycophancy? Our revered ones are being insulted. Those who are close to power are being given VIP treatment. Why this double standard? Question: What is your objection regarding UGC Regulation 2026? Answer: This regulation (January 13, 2026) is extremely discriminatory. It treats meritorious students from the general category as 'self-declared criminals'. They cannot be discriminated against. There is a high possibility of mental and physical exploitation of children through equality committees. Anyone can file a baseless complaint and ruin someone's future. Will we send our children to study in such a system where exploitation happens in the name of justice? I also want to ask those public representatives who take votes in the name of the Brahmin society and today sit silently like 'corporate employees'. Do you want the genocide of Brahmins? I want to ask MPs and MLAs - why are you wearing ankle bells, when will you speak up? Are you people waiting for our daughters and daughters-in-law to be raped on the streets? Are you waiting for orders from your masters? Will you speak only when the situation gets out of hand? You took tickets in the name of Brahmins. You took votes from Brahmins. Once you win, it doesn't matter anymore. Question: How do you see the future situation? Answer: Today, where is the upper caste society safe? Look at social media, across the country, the general category has separated from you. Both the central government and state government are minority governments. Today, neither democracy nor republic remains; this is just an 'illusion system'. Governments are in the minority and are running only on the policy of 'divide and rule'. BJP is no longer Indian; it has become like a 'Foreign People's Party'. I have resigned for this reason so that a message goes out that the general category is no longer with you. I have sent my resignation to the Governor, District Magistrate, and Election Commission (as ERO). Question: What do you want now? Answer: I am taking this step with Lord Bajrangbali as my witness. Now is the time for society and officials to boycott this injustice like a 'non-cooperation movement'. If we don't wake up today, future generations will never forgive us. The situation has become like a civil war. The future strategy will be decided by our Brahmin community's MLAs, MPs, and our society on what needs to be done next. That's why I have done this with Lord Bajrangbali as my witness. Now know about Alankar Agnihotri Alankar Agnihotri is from Kanpur. His father passed away in his childhood. Mother worked in a bank. In 1998, Alankar secured 21st rank in UP Board's 12th examination. After this, he completed B.Tech from Banaras Hindu University and started working. In 2014, when all of Alankar's younger brothers were settled, and his sister was married, he quit his job to prepare for the UPPCS and qualified for the exam in 2019.

stories.summary: A fight and stone-pelting occurred between students of two hostels at BHU (Banaras Hindu University) on Thursday. In the incident, PG student Piyush Tiwari sustained serious head injuries. He has been referred to the Trauma Center. It is alleged that expelled students Darshit Pandey, Raunak Mishra, Ankit Pal, and Vishwajeet Yadav assaulted Piyush Tiwari at the gate of Ruiya Hostel. After the incident, there was chaos in the hostel. Upon receiving information, Inspector Lanka Rajkumar Sharma and BHU Outpost In-charge Saurabh Tiwari arrived at the scene with forces. They pacified the agitated students. The agitated students are demanding action against the accused. Seeing the students' anger, 500 policemen, including DCP Kashi Gaurav, are conducting a search operation in the hostel. Surveillance is being done with drones. One fleeing student has been apprehended and taken for questioning. According to the Chief Proctor, 11 rooms of Birla-C Hostel have been sealed. Some suspicious items have also been found here. 4 pictures

stories.title: Bully drives gypsy with man on bonnet for 15 minutes:Starts spinning vehicle as people chase him in Rampur; video surfaces
stories.summary: In Rampur, a youth drove a Gypsy with an e-rickshaw driver stuck on its bonnet for about 200 metres, even spinning the vehicle in circles as people chased him to rescue the victim. The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon at Kemri Tirahe on the Bilaspur Highway, and a video has surfaced. The speeding Gypsy had first hit the e-rickshaw, injuring the driver. When the injured man stood in front of the vehicle to stop it, the driver instead accelerated, throwing him onto the bonnet and driving for nearly 15 minutes before stopping. Police have registered a case against the accused Gypsy driver. 3 pictures Read the full story Police sent the accused to ADM Court The e-rickshaw driver could have lost his life in the incident, but instead of taking strict action, the police took action under the section for disturbing the peace. Driving a vehicle negligently and endangering life (Rash Driving) falls under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which carries a punishment of up to 6 months in jail or a fine. In this case, Kotwali Station House Officer Balwan Singh informed that the arrested accused is Manpreet Singh, a resident of Sant Colony locality in the city. Action has been taken against him under sections for disturbing the peace. He has been sent to the SDM Court.

stories.title: Setback for Brij Bhushan Singh:Delhi High Court pulls up counsel, allows trial court hearing to go on, trouble deepens for former MP
stories.summary: The troubles of Uttar Pradesh strongman leader and former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh have not eased. In the sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers, the Delhi High Court on Thursday ruled that the trial court proceedings will continue and refused to stay the hearing. The court also reprimanded Brij Bhushan Singh’s counsel during the proceedings. Brij Bhushan Singh had approached the Delhi High Court seeking a stay on the trial court proceedings related to the FIR and charges framed against him. However, a bench headed by Justice Swarna Kanta Sharma declined to grant any interim relief and directed that the matter continue in the lower court. The High Court has now listed the case for further hearing on April 21. Brij Bhusan's lawyer sought adjournment During the hearing, Brij Bhushan Singh’s lawyer sought an adjournment, citing the absence of the main counsel. The court, however, rejected the request and made it clear that the trial should proceed without delay. The case is currently being heard at the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi. Court expressed displeasure with lawyer Justice Swarna Kanta said- Why haven't you been arguing until now? You have filed this petition, but it hasn't been presented for argument even once so far. Brijbhushan's lawyer assured the court that at the next hearing they will present their senior lawyer in court for arguments. The court warned that if there is no argument at the next hearing, the petition could be dismissed. The court said, ‘It is clarified that there is no stay on trial court proceedings.’ Brij Bhushan's claim - False allegations were made Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh had said in the High Court in 2024 that he was implicated in false allegations. He alleged that the investigation was biased and only the statements of the victims were given importance, while the truth of the allegations was not investigated. FIR was registered on Supreme Court's order In May 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR against Brij Bhushan after Supreme Court's intervention. On May 21, 2024, the trial court framed charges against him for sexual harassment, criminal intimidation and outraging the modesty of women. Co-accused and former WFI Assistant Secretary Vinod Tomar was also charged with criminal intimidation. 6 wrestlers made allegations On January 18, 2023, 6 wrestlers made sexual harassment allegations against former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The women wrestlers demanded action against Brij Bhushan from Union Sports Minister Anurag Thakur. When no action was taken at the government level in this matter, male and female wrestlers held a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar for more than six months. Acquitted in sexual exploitation case of minor wrestler Delhi's Patiala House Court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual exploitation case of a minor wrestler on May 26, 2025, and closed the case. In this case, the minor had retracted from her statement. After which the court took this decision. After the sexual exploitation case was closed, Brij Bhushan's close associates celebrated in Gonda. During the in-camera hearing on August 1, 2023, the minor had said that she made these allegations under political or emotional pressure. No such incident had occurred where she considered herself a victim. After this statement, the court considered it as 'serious variable evidence'. Brij Bhushan had said - There was no truth in the case Dainik Bhaskar had spoken to former MP Brij Bhushan over phone about the court's decision. He had said - This is the blessing of Bajrangbali and Lord Ram that I got my first major victory in this case. The minor wrestler had made allegations against me due to instigation by alleged wrestlers. But when she learned the truth, she gave the correct statement. Based on which the court has dismissed that case.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Supreme Court stays UGC's new regulations Supreme Court put a hold on the University Grants Commission (UGC)’s new rules until further orders. The bench of CJI Suryakant and Justice Joymalya said the provisions are unclear and could be misused. 2. UP cabinet approves cashless healthcare for 10 lakh teachers Ahead of Assembly elections, the UP Cabinet approved a cashless healthcare scheme for over 10 lakh teachers and education staff, including Shiksha Mitras, with a treatment limit of ₹5 lakh. The decision was taken in a Cabinet meeting chaired by CM Yogi Adityanath, which cleared 29 major proposals. 3. Elderly man commits suicide over unpaid electricity bill in Shahjahanpur An elderly man allegedly died by suicide over unpaid electricity dues of ₹32,000 in Shahjahanpur. A handwritten note addressed to CM Yogi Adityanath requested a waiver of his bills and asked authorities not to trouble his children after his death. 4. Ajit Pawar cremated in Maharashtra's Baramati with full-state honours Ajit Pawar was cremated with full state honours at Vidya Pratishthan ground, Baramati, around 12:15 pm on Thursday. His family, including wife Sunetra, sons Parth and Jai, Sharad Pawar, and Supriya Sule attended. Political leaders present included Amit Shah, Nitin Gadkari and Raj Thackeray. 5. Two prisoners escape Ayodhya jail after wall breach Two inmates in a special cell of Ayodhya District Jail escaped overnight by uprooting 30 bricks, triggering a major security alert. Following the incident, seven officials, including the jailer, were suspended. 6. Administration shuts 30 spa centres after Gorakhpur gangrape Following the gangrape of a 13-year-old girl in Gorakhpur, authorities suspended six police officers and shut down 30 illegal spa centres. The girl had posted an Instagram reel before leaving her colony, prompting swift action against the exploitation network. 7. India's GDP growth projected at 6.8-7.2% for FY27 Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Economic Survey 2025-26 in Parliament on 29 January 2026. The survey estimates India’s GDP growth at 6.8-7.2% for FY27, slightly lower than the 7.4% projected for the current fiscal year, according to sources. 8. Shankaracharya leaves Magh Mela suddenly after conflict with administration Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati abruptly left the Magh Mela on January 28 after an 11-day conflict with the Prayagraj administration. Officials said a closed-door meeting was held hours earlier; they expressed regret, but the Shankaracharya insisted on an apology before leaving. 9. Rs 71 lakh fraud in Kanpur fake IAS marriage case In Kanpur, a man posed as a bank officer and claimed to be selected for IAS, luring a young woman with marriage promises. He extorted about ₹71 lakh, including cash and jewelry, before being caught and sent to jail. 10. Jamaat leader dies in B'desh pre-election clash with BNP activists A Jamaat-e-Islami leader died at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital after being injured in a clash with BNP activists in Sherpur. The deceased, Maulana Md Rezaul Karim was the secretary of Jamaat’s Sreebordi upazila unit.

The accused allegedly knocked the victim to the ground, ran a Thar SUV over him, and deliberately left the vehicle stationary on his body for several minutes. Eyewitnesses said the victim lay trapped under the vehicle, groaning in pain, while the accused refused to move the Thar forward. As a result of the assault, the businessman’s leg was fractured at three places, leaving him unable to walk. He later lost consciousness and regained it only during treatment at the hospital. The victim’s friend, who was present at the scene, also sustained serious injuries to his head and ears and is currently undergoing medical treatment. Both accused out on bail in 1 day The incident occurred on the night of January 22 in the parking area of the Summit Building. Despite the gravity of the incident, both accused were granted bail within a day. Initially, police invoked sections related to breach of peace, though a case has also been registered under attempt to murder provisions. Speaking to Bhaskar, the victim alleged that the attackers kept the Thar parked on top of him for nearly 25 minutes, worsening his injuries. Police officials said the matter is under investigation, and statements of the victims and witnesses have been recorded. See pictures... Read sequence of events... Pawan Patel, originally from Fatehpur, currently resides in New Gudora in Sarojininagar and runs a building material business. He told Bhaskar that a few of his friends had come from the village, and at their request, he took them out for a late-night outing on January 22. According to Pawan, the group was partying at King Club in the Summit Building along with his friend Prashant Sachan and others. At around 1 am, when they stepped out of the parking area to leave in their cars, they noticed a group of youths in a Thar SUV and another car arguing among themselves on the premises. Pawan said he tried to intervene and calm the situation along with his friends. However, this reportedly angered the youths, who began abusing and assaulting them. During the altercation, the accused allegedly attempted to snatch Prashant Sachan’s chain and then ran the Thar over him. Bullies kept Thar mounted for 25 minutes Pawan said that during the scuffle with Prashant, he somehow managed to move away from the spot to save himself. Meanwhile, other companions arrived and tried to understand and defuse the situation, but the accused youths continued abusing them. Fearing further violence, Pawan and his friends ran outside to seek help. He said they asked the security guard to close the gate. At that moment, the Thar driven by the accused allegedly rammed into them from behind, causing him to fall to the ground. The assailants then reversed the vehicle and deliberately ran it over him. According to Pawan, the Thar remained parked on both his legs for nearly 25 minutes, during which he cried out in pain. He eventually lost consciousness and does not recall what happened next. He regained consciousness only after being admitted to the hospital. Leg bone broken from 3 places Pawan said that in the incident, his leg bone was broken from 3 places. It has a temporary plaster cast. The other leg also has serious injuries. That leg remains swollen. He is walking with the help of a walker. Doctors have advised to apply permanent plaster after 4 days. We were beaten up in someone else's dispute Pawan's friend Prashant Sachan said that they were returning after a party. Two groups were having a dispute on the way. There was difficulty in passing through there. When we objected to this, the bullies attacked us. We came out from a different club and the accused boys came from another club. They started fighting with people to take revenge for someone else's dispute. The goons came in two cars. There was also a Swift Dzire involved in the incident. The Thar was stopped by closing the gate but the Dzire occupants escaped. Police arrested Akash Yadav and Mohit Mewadi, residents of Rudrapur, Uttarakhand, from the spot. Questions raised on police working style There is a police post adjacent to gate number 4 of the Summit Building, which would be barely 30 meters from the incident site. Despite this, the accused had no fear. The parking dispute continued for about half an hour, but the police didn't even know about it. However, police claim that the club is closed at 12 AM. The internal security clears the entire parking from 12:30 to 1 AM. This incident has raised questions about police functioning. Inspector Vibhutikhand Amar Singh said that a report has been filed based on the victim's complaint. The Thar used in the incident has been seized. Raids are being conducted to search for other absconding accused.

stories.title: 'Keshav Maurya failed to take a stand' says Avimukteshwaranand:Shankaracharya questions govt silence over Magh Mela incident
stories.summary: 'If someone says they will go only when they are sent, it means they lack independent judgement. A discerning person takes decisions by assessing the situation themselves. Here, government representatives should have taken a clear stand, which they failed to do.' These remarks were made by Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati after returning to Kashi from Prayagraj, while speaking to the media. He was responding to a statement made by Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya during the Magh Mela protest. The Deputy CM had said that the Chief Minister had taken cognisance of the matter and that he would speak when asked, pray if required, and bow at the feet if needed. ‘Insult to Shankaracharya is direct insult to Sanatan’ The Shankaracharya referred to Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s statement that governments which insult Sanatan do not return to power. He said that in Prayagraj, Brahmacharis, Batuks, saints, householders, and devotees who came for Sangam Snan were insulted. Since the Shankaracharya himself represents Sanatan, his humiliation amounts to a direct insult to Sanatan Dharma. He added that had the government abandoned its arrogance and corrected its mistake in time, the situation would not have escalated. Akhilesh Yadav’s statement shows issue goes beyond religion Commenting on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks, the Shankaracharya said that when political leaders themselves are calling the incident unfortunate, it is clear that the matter is not merely religious but is also linked to governance and sensitivity. ‘Denial of Sangam Snan Was Unthinkable’ Avimukteshwaranand described his inability to take the Sangam Snan as unfortunate and unimaginable. He said that despite being given opportunities continuously for 11 days, the failure to correct the mistake was deeply distressing. He explained that in Sanatan tradition, a yagna is not considered complete until the Purnahuti is performed. It was traditionally believed that the collective snan of Sanatan followers is completed only after the Shankaracharya’s snan. This time, he said, the Purnahuti did not take place. See 3 photos- ‘UGC’s new act will divide society’ Upon arriving in Kashi, the Shankaracharya performed formal worship at the Math and held an important meeting with the saint community. Serious discussions took place on the cow protection movement and recent developments. Speaking on the controversy related to the UGC, he said it is not an issue of any single political party but one that divides society. Pitting one caste against another and encouraging internal conflict weakens Hindu society. He alleged that what is said on public platforms is contradicted by actual conduct. 'On stage, slogans like ‘Bantoge toh katoge’ are raised, but in practice, machines to divide and destroy are being brought in,' he said. ‘Governments not serious about stopping cow slaughter’ The Shankaracharya said that governments at both the Centre and state levels are not serious about stopping cow slaughter. He alleged that those who raise the issue are deliberately silenced. He clearly stated that Sanatan tradition is not run by any government, leader, or political party. “Attempts will be made to silence us, but we will not stop. Every Sanatani must now join the movement to protect Gomata. We are not concerned with who is in power or which party governs,” he said. ‘Allegations must be proven, mere claims are not enough’ Avimukteshwaranand said that organisations like the Vishva Hindu Raksha Parishad had put up posters against him in Raebareli, calling him a ‘Kalyugi Ravan’ and even a Pakistani agent. He said such allegations must be proven, as mere statements mean nothing. He added that whatever he says is backed by logic and evidence. Questions raised on police action and lack of inquiry Referring to the Magh Mela unrest, he said the complete truth has still not emerged and the public has seen only a fraction of what happened. Had the full video surfaced, the picture would have been entirely different. Questioning the police role, he asked whether reprimanding one policeman and suspending another amounts to justice. He pointed out that no independent inquiry committee was formed. Anger over silence of centre and state governments On the question of central intervention, he said that when something is wrong, hierarchy becomes irrelevant. Right must be called right and wrong must be called wrong, but in this case, no one is speaking. He said that after the incident, he waited peacefully for 11 days, hoping corrective action would be taken. He believed initially it might have been a local administrative lapse, but no concrete action followed even after such a serious matter. Clarification on unity of 4 Shankaracharyas Addressing confusion regarding the unity of the four Shankaracharyas, Avimukteshwaranand said a false narrative is being spread that they are divided. He asserted that all four Shankaracharyas have always been united. He said those claiming otherwise are spreading misinformation. In the recent events, all four Shankaracharyas stood together. He emphasised that Shankaracharyas hold the highest position in Sanatan tradition and their role should not be undermined. Call for probe into Maharashtra Plane Crash On the death of Ajit Pawar in the Maharashtra plane crash, the Shankaracharya said such tragic incidents must be investigated impartially and thoroughly. He said the nature of the inquiry should ensure the truth comes out and no confusion or suspicion remains. What has happened so far?

stories.title: Jaish-e-Mohammed, Al-Qaeda linked terrorist drew up hit list of 7:People from Delhi UP included in list, police procure weapons for public killings
stories.summary: On January 25, 2026, Gujarat ATS arrested a suspicious youth from the Charpul area of Navsari. The arrested accused was identified as Faizan Sheikh, who is originally from Rampur, Uttar Pradesh and was currently living in Navsari, where he worked as a tailor. Faizan Sheikh had come under the influence of terrorist organizations and was planning to spread terror in the country. For this, he had also purchased a pistol and six cartridges. Faizan Sheikh had prepared a list of people who made statements against Islam and the Prophet and planned to kill them. Faizan had made a list of seven people, which has been obtained by ATS. Faizan had also made controversial posts about killing these seven people in such a way that the world would watch. Literature of 29 pages found in Urdu and Arabic language Faizan was also in contact with terrorists from terrorist organizations like Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba and admitted that he was ready to carry out any incident at their direction. However, ATS caught him before this intention could be fulfilled. Literature of 29 pages in Urdu and Arabic language was also recovered from him. Faizan made a list of seven people ATS begins investigation of Faizan's phone details Along with this, the list was also forwarded in a specific group and mentioned that these people would be killed in a way for the world to see. Additionally, the ATS team has started investigating all the details of Faizan's phone. They have begun a detailed investigation of who he was connected with on social media. Was influenced by radical ideology of Jaish-e-Mohammed and Al-Qaeda ATS investigation has revealed that Faizan Sheikh was influenced by the radical ideology of banned terrorist organizations Jaish-e-Mohammed and Al-Qaeda. After being radicalized through online media and other means, he had targeted specific groups of people with the intention of spreading fear and creating chaos in society. Gujarat ATS reached where the terrorist was picked up from. During his interrogation, it was found that he was following Masood Azhar and was collecting data on those who made statements against the Prophet. He had bought weapons from the money he earned by sewing clothes. Accused prepared a list of prominent people from UP The accused was associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed group. He had been living in Navsari for the last 4 years and worked as a tailor. He was running groups on Instagram and Telegram. The accused had started targeting people who spoke against Prophet Mohammed. The accused had prepared a list of prominent people from UP. The accused has not attacked anyone so far. The accused used to follow terrorist Masood Azhar A person named Abu Bakar was associated with the accused, who is under investigation. The accused used to make plans on Instagram and Telegram to kill those who spoke against the Prophet and would share these plans with others. The accused also used to follow terrorist Masood Azhar. He would collect online data of people who made statements against the Prophet. Faizan Sheikh had been working as a tailor in Navsari for the past few years Faizan Sheikh was currently living in the Charpul area of Navsari and is originally from Dundawala, Narpat Nagar in Rampur district of Uttar Pradesh. He had been earning his livelihood by working as a tailor in Navsari for the past few years, where large-scale job work is done and craftsmen from Uttar Pradesh work.

stories.title: Fake IAS cheats woman of ₹71 lakh in Kanpur:Accused Nitesh Pandey promises marriage and blackmails her, takes jewellery and cash; arrested
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a cunning young man first trapped a young woman in a love affair by introducing himself as a government bank officer. After this, he claimed to have been selected for IAS. He lured the girl with the promise of marriage. He said that he needed millions of rupees for the selection and asked for money. On this, the girl gave him about 71 lakh rupees, including cash and jewelry. The cunning young man assured her of joining IAS by sending fake emails, joining letters, and documents on WhatsApp from a mail ID similar to a government department's website. Police have arrested the accused Nitesh Pandey. Know the full case in detail Took ₹ 26.50 lakh cash and ₹45 lakh worth of Jewelry The young woman residing in Kalyanpur used to work in a media organization. Her father is a clerk in the municipal corporation. She has two brothers. Her mother has passed away. Her brothers run a shop under the name Mamta Artificial. After her mother's death, the girl herself used to keep the house's money and jewelry etc. The girl's brother said - money had been collected and kept for the shop and his sister's wedding. The jewelry was also with his sister. Cunning Nitesh Pandey gave the pretext of marriage. He demanded millions of rupees in the name of selection in IAS. The sister gave the jewelry and cash kept at home. Nitesh first took 26.50 lakh rupees in cash. After this, he also swindled gold and silver jewelry worth approximately 45 lakh rupees. The victim girl said - Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam of Shuklaganj is a family friend. Through him, she met Nitesh Pandey, a resident of Chakeri. Nitesh first introduced himself as a Field Officer in a government bank, then claimed to be an SDM, and later claimed selection in IAS. The young man started distancing himself after taking money Nitesh deceived her, saying he would marry her after completing his IAS training. Therefore, the girl completely trusted him. The young man gradually started distancing himself. When she became suspicious and asked for her money back, he procrastinated by giving a fake check. Threatened with a knife, said he would implicate her in a false case It is alleged that when the young woman asked for money and threatened to file a police case, the young man Nitesh started blackmailing her. He threatened to kill her. He threatened to viral her private pictures. On October 14, 2025, the young woman had gone to the house of Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam. It is alleged that here Nitesh Pandey threatened her with a knife. He abused her. He threatened to kill the entire family and implicate them in false cases. FIR against four accused, main accused arrested late at night On the application of the victim girl, Kalyanpur police station registered an FIR against four accused on Wednesday. Police have registered a report against Nitesh Pandey, Diwakar Mishra alias Satyam, Jitesh Pandey and Akanksha Pandey. Accused Nitesh Pandey is an MA pass in Psychology. His father and mother have passed away; his father was retired from the Air Force. He lives with his brother and sister-in-law.

stories.title: Illegal dairy operators hide animals in bedrooms:LMC recovers buffaloes and goats after 3-hour raid in Lucknow
stories.summary: A bizarre scene unfolded in Lucknow when buffaloes and goats were found hidden inside a house’s bedroom during a municipal corporation drive against illegal dairies. The incident occurred in Bijnor area of Zone-8, where a team of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) had arrived to take action against unlawfully operating dairy units. As soon as the civic team reached Royal City Colony in Gadora, dairy operators attempted to evade action by locking their animals inside residential houses. In one such case, a dairy owner confined buffaloes and goats inside a room of his house, turning bedrooms and drawing rooms into makeshift cattle shelters. Drive conducted for 3 hours LMC officials faced stiff resistance from locals, and their vehicles were also surrounded during the operation. Despite the obstruction, the team continued the drive and, after nearly three hours of sustained effort, managed to remove the animals from inside the houses. Officials said that several buffaloes and cows were recovered from living spaces, highlighting the extent to which illegal dairy operators had encroached upon residential areas. The action was carried out to curb unhygienic conditions and violations caused by illegal dairies in the locality. See pictures... During the operation, the municipal corporation seized a total of 11 buffaloes, four heifers, three cows and one calf. All the animals have been shifted to the Aishbagh Kanji House, where they will remain detained until the prescribed penalty is paid, officials said. The action was initiated following repeated complaints from local residents, who alleged that illegal dairy operators were dumping animal dung in open plots and discharging waste into sewer lines. This had led to severe filth, waterlogging and an increased risk of mosquito-borne diseases in the area. Buffalo rearing prohibited in city limits The Municipal Corporation clarified that under the Municipal Corporation Act, 1959, rearing of buffaloes is completely banned within urban limits, as buffaloes are classified as pollution-causing animals. As per rules, residents are permitted to keep a maximum of two cows, and that too only with a valid license. Joint operation by multiple departments The enforcement drive was carried out with the joint participation of the police force, municipal enforcement team and the animal welfare department. Animal Welfare Officer Dr Abhinav Verma said that strict action against illegally operating dairies will continue in the coming days. At the spot, special assistance was provided by team members Manoj, Ramkumar, Furkan and Nadeem, who played a key role in successfully carrying out the operation despite resistance.

stories.title: Former Bareilly Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri reaches Lucknow:At in-laws’ house, says, 'Bajrangbali’s blessings are with me and I will not seek security'
stories.summary: Former Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, who had resigned from the post citing UP government misbehaving with Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand during Magh Mela, reached Lucknow late on Wednesday night. He was dropped at his in-laws' house in Alambagh, where there was strict police vigil throughout the night. Upon reaching Lucknow, PCS officer Alankar told reporters, "Bajrangbali's blessings are with me. I will not ask for security." He further said, "The Bareilly administration has sent me to Lucknow in a planned manner. I was externed on an oral order. There was no concrete incident in Bareilly that would have necessitated my removal from there. The government has the right to accept or reject the resignation, but I was deliberately not allowed to stay in Bareilly." Meanwhile, his new tweet has surfaced. In it, he has appealed to all general category organizations, all sections of society, and various farmer unions to unite. He wrote on X, "Now is the time to consider a new alternative in which all sections have proper representation." People are rapidly sharing it with hashtags #Mera_CM_Mera_Beta and #savarn_ekta. According to the information, Alankar Agnihotri will go from Lucknow to Etah and Hathras. He will participate in the ongoing protests against UGC. He will strategize with his supporters. After three days, he will return to Bareilly. He says that UGC's new rules will turn upper-caste students into self-proclaimed criminals. They will close the doors of higher education. He will not bow down at any cost. Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati called him with blessings Alankar Agnihotri stated that he had prominently raised the issue of alleged insult to Sanatan culture during the Magh Mela. In this regard, he had a conversation with Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati. He received blessings from Shankaracharya and was also invited to visit the ashram, which he has accepted. Regarding his next step, Alankar Agnihotri said that he will now further strengthen his strategy. He is in contact with various organizations associated with the upper caste community. He also alleged that many elected representatives, regardless of which community they belong to, are not fulfilling their responsibilities. They become active only upon receiving orders, like corporate employees. If Brahmins were assaulted, where were the public representatives? When his resignation was called a political move, Alankar Agnihotri said that when symbols of Sanatan culture were being attacked and incidents of assault against Batuk Brahmins came to light, why were the concerned public representatives silent then? He also mentioned the UGC guidelines published on January 13, which raised objections regarding the 'Swarn Samaj' (upper caste community) in categories related to caste-based discrimination. He stated that such a system is causing innocent people to be viewed as criminals. ‘Opposition leaders contacted, they agreed with me’ Alankar Agnihotri said that representatives of various national and regional political parties have contacted him and expressed sympathy. He said that he received a call from Mata Prasad Pandey, Leader of Opposition in the UP Assembly, who affirmed the correctness of the issues he raised and offered support. On the question asked about the police force present with him, Alankar Agnihotri said that providing security or not is the decision of the district and police administration. He said that if the administration deems it necessary, security will be provided, there is no need to make a separate demand for it. He expressed confidence that Bajrangbali's blessings are with him and whatever God wills, will happen. Know what has happened so far

stories.title: Grandmother recalls Pinky’s smile after loss:Jaunpur flight attendant visited home 2 months ago; passed away along with Maha Dy CM Ajit Pawar in plane crash
stories.summary: Grief has engulfed Bhainsa village in Uttar Pradesh’s Jaunpur district after Pinki Mala, a flight attendant originally from the area, lost her life in a plane crash involving late Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar in Pune. Pinki, who lived in Pune with her husband, was among those killed when the chartered aircraft crashed during landing at Baramati airport on Wednesday morning. Her 80-year-old grandmother, Maharaji, recalled Pinki as a cheerful and warm-hearted young woman. Fighting back tears, she said she still remembers her granddaughter’s smiling face. “She was so happy and full of life. In old age, this is the sorrow we are left to see,” she said. Body handed over to family, last rites to be performed in Pune Pinki’s mortal remains have been handed over to her family. Her parents rushed to Pune as soon as they received news of the crash. Her father, Shivkumar Mali, said the body has been brought to their residence in Pune, where the last rites will be performed. After the funeral, her ashes will be immersed in Varanasi. The family has asked relatives in Jaunpur not to travel to Pune for now. Pinki’s parents have been living in Mumbai’s Worli area for several years, while the extended family resides in Jaunpur. News of her death plunged the village into mourning. ‘My son is like a madman now’: Grandmother recounts the moment she heard the news Recalling the moment she learned about the tragedy, Pinki’s grandmother said she was at a temple in her daughter-in-law’s village when locals informed her about the crash. She immediately called her son, Shivkumar, who was in Pune. “He was crying uncontrollably. He just said he didn’t know where Pinki had gone and disconnected the call,” she said. Every eye in the village is moist, see the pictures... Plane crashed during landing at Baramati airport The accident occurred around 8:45 am on Wednesday when the chartered plane carrying Ajit Pawar crashed while landing at Baramati airport. The Deputy Chief Minister was traveling to address a public meeting related to the Maharashtra Panchayat elections. The crash claimed the lives of five people, including Pawar, his security personnel, two pilots, and flight attendant Pinki Mali. Pinki’s home village Bhainsa is about 40 km from the Jaunpur district headquarters. Villagers learned about the crash nearly two hours later through television news channels. Repeated attempts to contact Pinki’s parents initially failed, adding to the anxiety and shock. Relatives remember Pinki as bright, friendly, and intelligent Pinki’s uncle Rajkumar Mali described her as a bright and sociable young woman. “She was intelligent and very understanding. All her education was in Mumbai. She wasn’t just our niece; she was like a daughter to us,” he said, adding that she had visited the village around two-and-a-half months ago. Her uncle Chandrabhushan Mali recalled seeing her briefly about two months ago. “She had come for just half an hour. She was smiling and cheerful. We never imagined this would be the last time we would see her,” he said. Village resident Ashok Singh said Pinki’s father had deep ties with the village and used to organize Durga Puja every year. He had visited the village again just two months earlier. Journey to becoming a flight attendant Pinki Mali was the eldest among three siblings—two sisters and a brother. Her grandfather, Baburam, the head of the family, passed away last year. Her siblings, Preeti and Karan, live in Mumbai. According to the family, Pinki completed her intermediate studies from Tulsi Mank College in Dadar, Mumbai, and later pursued a course to become an air hostess. She worked for nearly four years at Mumbai International Airport before serving as a flight attendant on chartered aircraft for the past five years. Last conversation with her father Pinki’s father, Shivkumar Mali, who drives a taxi in Mumbai and is associated with the Shiv Sena, said he spoke to his daughter a day before the accident. “She was very happy. She told me on the phone, ‘Papa, today I have a flight with Ajit Pawar. I’ll make you talk to him,’” he recalled. “I never imagined that would be our last conversation.” Her brother Karan said Pinki had called him on Wednesday morning, informing him that she was traveling from Baramati to Nanded. “After that, there was no message or call,” he said. Mother’s premonition and Unbearable loss Pinki’s mother, Maya Mali, broke down upon hearing the news. She said she felt uneasy throughout the day, sensing that something was wrong. “My heart was restless, but no one was telling me clearly what had happened,” she said. She added that Pinki used to call her every morning without fail. “She would remind me to eat breakfast and take my medicines. That day, there was no call, no message. That hurt the most,” she said. Maya Mali said Pinki had worked with several prominent leaders and officials, including Ajit Pawar, Devendra Fadnavis, and Narayan Rane. “We were proud of her job,” she said, while demanding a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to determine whether it was due to technical failure or any other reason. Married in Ballia, family mourns across states Pinki’s cousin Sheetla Prasad Mali said the family had been living in Mumbai for the past 30–35 years due to work. Pinki was married in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh, and her in-laws live in Pune. The tragic incident has left both her marital and maternal families in deep mourning. As relatives and villagers struggle to come to terms with the loss, memories of Pinki’s warmth, dedication, and smile continue to linger—now as a painful reminder of a life cut short. 29-year-old Pinky was married in Ballia, but now her in-laws also lived in Pune.Pinky Mali with Maharashtra Deputy CM Ajit Pawar. (File photo)

stories.title: UP clears cashless healthcare for 10 lakh teachers:Shiksha Mitras included with ₹5 lakh treatment limit; Cabinet approves 29 major proposals
stories.summary: In a major welfare decision ahead of the Assembly elections, the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet on Thursday approved a cashless healthcare scheme for over 10 lakh teachers and education staff, including Shiksha Mitras, with a treatment limit of up to ₹5 lakh. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, where a total of 29 proposals were cleared. Cashless treatment for Teachers and Education staff Under the new scheme, teachers and employees of primary and secondary schools will be eligible for cashless medical treatment. This includes staff from aided and self-financed institutions, as well as schools run by the Basic Education Council. The benefit will extend to: Officials said the move will ensure that educators no longer have to worry about medical expenses during illness, whether routine or critical. CM’s Teacher’s Day promise fulfilled Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had announced the scheme on Teachers’ Day, stating that teachers should focus on educating children without worrying about healthcare costs. Thursday’s Cabinet approval formally implements that assurance. Key Urban and Infrastructure decisions Among other major decisions, the Cabinet approved: Science parks, Transport, and Industrial projects The Cabinet also cleared: Other major approvals Additional decisions include: Political significance Political observers view the Cabinet’s decisions—especially the cashless healthcare scheme for teachers—as a strategic move by the Yogi government to strengthen its support base among educators and government staff ahead of elections. Officials said implementation guidelines for the healthcare scheme will be issued soon, ensuring seamless rollout across the state.

stories.title: 2 prisoners escape Ayodhya jail after wall breach:Lodged in special cell, inmates uproot 30 bricks overnight; jailer among 7 officials suspended
stories.summary: Two prisoners lodged in the Ayodhya District Jail escaped after breaking through a wall of the prison’s special cell during the night, triggering a major security alert and administrative action. The escape came to light early Thursday morning during the routine headcount. The fugitives have been identified as Golu Agrahari alias Suraj and Sher Ali alias Rafiq Ali, both facing serious criminal charges including murder and rape. Dug through special cell wall, fled using makeshift rope According to police officials, both prisoners were confined in Cell No. 4 of Special Cell No. 1. The barracks were locked at around 6 PM on Wednesday, with both inmates present inside at the time. When prison staff began counting inmates at around 6 AM on Thursday, the two prisoners were found missing. A subsequent inspection revealed that 25 to 30 bricks had been removed from the iron-grilled rear wall of the cell. Investigators believe the inmates spent the entire night loosening the bricks. They then tied blankets and mufflers together to form a rope and climbed over a 20-foot-high boundary wall to escape. Officials suspect long-term planning Police officials said the method used to remove the bricks and the preparation of a rope indicate that the prisoners had been planning the jailbreak for a considerable period. A thorough search was conducted inside the jail premises, and CCTV footage was examined, but no immediate clues about their escape route were found. Escaped prisoners face multiple serious charges Senior jail officials suspended, inquiry ordered Taking serious note of the incident, Director General of Prisons P.C. Meena ordered strict action. The following officials have been suspended: A departmental inquiry has also been ordered to determine lapses in security and supervision. District officials inspect jail District Magistrate Nikhil Tikaram Funde and SSP Dr. Gaurav Grover visited the Ayodhya District Jail to inspect the site and review security arrangements. Senior officials questioned jail authorities and sought a detailed report on how the breach occurred. Police teams have been deployed to track down the escaped prisoners, and efforts are underway to trace their movements.

stories.title: 'Why only OBC?' General category students protest UGC 2026 rules:Lucknow University students split as UGC equity guidelines spark debate
stories.summary: At Lucknow University, tensions are rising among students over the new University Grants Commission (UGC) rules, the Equity in Higher Education Regulations 2026. While the regulations aim to eliminate discrimination and ensure equal opportunities for students from marginalized communities, General Category students claim the rules neglect their concerns. Harsh Mishra, a first-year MA student, said, “We face discrimination too. We are mocked as ‘Churki Wala’ and targeted for our caste. If rules exist for OBC and other communities, why not for General Category students?” Since the notification of UGC 2026, General Category students have staged protests across the university campus, from classrooms to administrative corridors, expressing frustration over perceived inequities. Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Lucknow University and spoke to general students about their issues and problems, their perspective on the dispute with OBC, and to professors about their concerns. Read the report… “Born villains” – students speak Bhaskar reporters visited the campus and witnessed students raising slogans against the UGC guidelines. About 100 General Category students gathered, highlighting their sense of exclusion. Student leader Jatin Shukla explained, “The UGC rules categorize students without surveys or consultations with teachers. It seems General Category students are being treated as ‘born villains.’” He added, “We study, live, and eat together, yet OBC, SC-ST, and EWS students are grouped separately. This creates unnecessary divisions among students who previously coexisted without concern for caste.” Akhilesh Mishra, another General Category student, commented, “These guidelines appear aimed at fostering caste-based conflict rather than addressing actual discrimination. There is no mention of biases against General Category students in the rules, raising serious questions.” Professors call protests political Professors at the university describe the student protests differently. Professor Suresh Bahadur said, “The government designed these rules after studying various case studies and experiences to curb caste-based discrimination at both student and teacher levels. The regulations will bring positive change, though much depends on mindset.” Professor Anitya Gaurav added, “Those opposing the rules may not fully understand their provisions. The guidelines aim to protect economically weaker sections, differently-abled students, and women, regardless of caste or religion. The opposition seems politically motivated rather than social.” OBC students support the rules Meanwhile, OBC students have voiced support for the regulations. Shailendra Yadav said, “We must consider the context of incidents like Rohit Vemula. Marginalised students face extreme pressures due to discrimination, sometimes leading to tragedies. The new rules aim to prevent such cases.” Yadav acknowledged that poor General Category students also face challenges, but argued that the guidelines were primarily intended to address recurring issues affecting marginalised communities. Amitesh Pal, another OBC student, said, “There may be some flaws, but overall, the rules are necessary. They extend protections similar to laws already in place for SC-ST students and will help prevent discrimination in educational institutions.” Legal provisions for marginalised communities UGC’s 2026 regulations require all higher education institutions to establish Equal Opportunity Centres. Special committees will address complaints regarding discrimination, and a 24-hour helpline will be set up. Institutions must respond to complaints within a set timeframe, or face penalties. SC, ST, OBC, women, and specially-abled students are explicitly protected under these rules. Critics argue that by focusing on these groups, General Category students are being unfairly excluded and labelled as potential perpetrators of discrimination. Confusion and Misunderstanding On campus, some students remain unclear about the rules. Several admitted they had not read the UGC draft and were unsure about its provisions. Confusion has fueled protests and debates, with some believing the rules penalise General Category students, while others understand they aim to protect marginalized students. Social implications Sociologists note that the protests reflect broader social changes. Breakdowns of joint families, increased economic independence for women, and heightened awareness of individual rights are shifting attitudes. Where earlier family or societal pressure ensured compliance in relationships, students now seek legal safeguards. The debate raises questions about trust and equality within educational institutions. Some argue that labeling students as potential violators undermines trust, while others see the rules as essential protections for vulnerable communities. Political fallout in Uttar Pradesh UGC 2026 has sparked protests across Uttar Pradesh. In cities including Lucknow and Varanasi, General Category students and sections of society have taken to the streets. In Bareilly, City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri resigned in protest, followed by resignations from more than six BJP leaders.

stories.title: Administration shuts 30 spa centres following Gorakhpur gangrape incident:13-year-old posted Instagram reel before leaving colony; 6 cops suspended for negligence
stories.summary: Following the horrific gang rape of a 13-year-old girl in Gorakhpur, authorities have taken swift action, suspending six police officers and shutting down numerous illegal spa centers. The case has exposed a disturbing network of exploitation and negligence, prompting a widespread crackdown. Police negligence leads to suspension of officers The initial response to the girl's disappearance and subsequent ordeal was met with criticism, leading to the suspension of six police personnel, including the station in-charge of Gorakhnath police station. The suspended officers include: Crackdown on illegal spa centers On Wednesday, police teams conducted raids across the city, targeting spa centers operating without proper licenses. Over 30 spa centers were shut down with immediate effect. Police have warned that regular monitoring will be conducted, and the operation will extend to all police station areas within the district. Additionally, authorities in Barhalganj held meetings with hotel owners, issuing warnings about strict adherence to regulations. Boards have been removed from hotels owned by Dhirendra Singh, a key accused in the gang rape, and steps are being taken to seal the properties. Victim's story and Social Media influence According to sources, the 13-year-old girl went missing on January 1st. Witnesses reported seeing her making a reel on her mobile phone in front of a temple before getting into a van. The girl's mother reported the incident to the Gorakhnath police station. Further investigation revealed that the victim had become infatuated with a 15-year-old barber she met on Instagram. Described as wanting to live a luxurious life, she idolized the high-profile lifestyles she saw on social media. Despite dropping out of school after the 5th grade, she spoke English well due to her constant activity on Instagram. She referred to her boyfriend as "BF My Jaan" in her social media posts. Details of the crime After running away from home, the girl stayed in a hotel in Karimnagar with her Instagram friend, where she was allegedly raped. Hotel owner Abhay alias Dhirendra Singh then sent her to a spa center in Betiyahaata and later to Barhalganj, where she was subjected to further sexual abuse. The girl was reportedly given intoxicating substances before the assaults. Arrests and Ongoing investigation So far, police have arrested hotel owner Abhay, hotel manager Adarsh Pandey, spa manager Ankit Kumar, the girl's social media friend, and one other individual. Authorities are actively searching for three additional suspects, including a partner of hotel owner Abhay, who is believed to have fled to Nepal. Victim's Plea for Justice In her statement to the court, the victim described how her trust was betrayed and how she was exploited. She pleaded for the strictest possible punishment for the accused. This is how the incident happened with the teenager Timeline of events Police response SSP Rajkaran Nayyar stated that accountability will be ensured at all levels and that the safety of the victim and the apprehension of the culprits are top priorities. He emphasized that any negligence will not be tolerated. 6 police personnel suspended Additional details Police sources indicate that the girl was kept in a hotel in GIDA, owned by a partner of Abhay, after falling ill at the spa center. The police recovered the girl from this hotel. The victim's family alleges that the police have not yet arrested the hotel owner or taken action against the hotel. Four police teams, including a surveillance team, are searching for the GIDA hotel owner and two other suspects.

stories.title: Why Kinnars perform Yoni Puja at Magh Mela:Aghori Kinnars cite Maa Kamakhya link; Mahamandaleshwar explains tantric ritual significance
stories.summary: Whether it is the Maha Kumbh or the ongoing Magh Mela in Prayagraj, one place that consistently draws large crowds is the Kinnar Akhara. This year, the Kinnar Akhara has been allotted camps at three different locations—a first in the history of the Magh Mela. A striking similarity connects all three camps: each has a perpetually lit Hawan Kund shaped like a Yoni (female reproductive organ). Devotees stop by, fold their hands in reverence, and move ahead quietly. The sight raises a common question among visitors—why do Kinnars worship the Yoni? To understand the belief behind this practice, the Dainik Bhaskar team visited the Kinnar Akhara and spoke to its Mahamandaleshwars, saints, and Aghori Kinnars. Three camps for the first time at Magh Mela This is the first time the Kinnar Akhara has been given three separate camps at the Magh Mela. At all three locations, the Hawan Kund used for worship has been constructed in the shape of a Yoni. “This is not a separate faith,” says Mahamandaleshwar Sanjana Nand Giri At the Sanatani Kinnar Akhada in Sector-6, Mahamandaleshwar Sanjana Nand Giri explained that the Kinnar community’s Kuldevi (clan goddess) is Bahuchara Mata. “It is not that our method of worship is separate. We follow all traditional rituals as well. It is incorrect to say we only perform Yoni worship,” she said. During the visit, rituals were being performed near the Kund, though video recording was not permitted. A form of Tantric Sadhana Mahamandaleshwar Kaushalya Nand Giri explained the spiritual philosophy behind the practice. “All life originates from the Yoni; that is why it holds special importance. One of the ten Mahavidyas is Tantric in nature, and this practice is linked to Tantra Sadhana,” she said. She added that many Kinnars who follow tantric paths perform such worship in the evenings or even throughout the night, especially during Gupt Navratri. Aghori Kinnar explains the Kamakhya connection Near the havan kund, an Aghori Kinnar was seen performing rituals. He explained that the Yoni-shaped Kund represents Goddess Kamakhya, one of the 51 Shakti Peeths and a central deity in Tantric traditions. “Wherever we perform worship, the structure is made in the form of the Yoni. It symbolizes Maa Kamakhya,” he said. He further explained that the kund is designed with three angles, symbolizing Maha Kali, Maha Saraswati, and Maha Lakshmi, along with the presence of Mahakal, Brahma, and Vishnu. Only grains such as wheat, chickpeas, lentils, and pulses are offered in the fire, as grains are considered the purest offering. Bahuchara Mata and Iravan: Deities of the Kinnar community The Kinnar community worships Bahuchara Mata as their Kuldevi. Her most famous temple is in Mehsana, Gujarat, where she is depicted riding a rooster and is worshipped in the form of Ardhanarishwara. The origins of Kinnar worship are also linked to the Mahabharata. Aravan (Iravan), son of Arjuna and Nagakanya Ulupi, is considered the kuldevta of the Kinnar community. According to legend, Lord Krishna took a transgender form to marry Iravan before his sacrifice to Goddess Kali. Even today, when a new member joins the Kinnar community, a symbolic marriage to Iravan is performed.

stories.title: Elderly man’s suicide over unpaid electricity bill in Shahjahanpur:Writes final note for CM Yogi, seeks waiver; ₹32,000 due, urges authorities not to trouble children after death
stories.summary: An elderly man died by alleged suicide after being distressed over unpaid electricity bills in Shahjahanpur district. According to the information, a handwritten suicide note addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was recovered from his pocket, in which he appealed for the waiver of his electricity dues and requested that his children not be harassed after his death. The incident took place in Nahil village under the Powayan police station area. The deceased has been identified as Kamendra Vikram Singh. Body found hanging from tree, police informed Villagers spotted Kamendra Vikram Singh’s body hanging from a tree on Wednesday afternoon and immediately informed the police. A police team reached the spot, recovered the body, and sent it for post-mortem examination. Senior officials, including the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) and Circle Officer (CO), also reached the scene. After counselling by police officials, the family consented to the post-mortem. ₹32,000 electricity bill dues, mental stress for months According to family members, Kamendra had been under mental stress for the past two to three months due to financial issues. He reportedly had an outstanding electricity bill of around Rs 32,000. The family said he had tried to avail benefits under the One Time Settlement (OTS) scheme to clear the dues but was unable to do so for unspecified reasons. Officials had reportedly advised him to pay Rs 17,000 in instalments, but the matter remained unresolved. On Wednesday afternoon, Kamendra left home and allegedly took the extreme step shortly thereafter. Suicide note mentions electricity dues and personal loans Police recovered a suicide note from the deceased’s pocket, addressed to the Chief Minister. In the note, Kamendra wrote that he was troubled by electricity dues and also mentioned a personal loan of around Rs 50,000. He reportedly wrote: Chief Minister, please waive my electricity bill. After my death, my children should not be troubled. The note also stated that his family members were unaware of the extent of his financial difficulties. Family background Kamendra lived with his wife in Nahil village. He is survived by two sons and one daughter, all of whom are married. His younger son, Saurabh Singh alias Aditya, works in a pesticide company and lived with his parents. His elder son, Achyut, is a private school teacher and lives separately with his wife in a rented house. Police statement Powayan Circle Officer Praveen Malik said the suicide note mentions distress due to electricity dues and loan burdens, adding that the deceased stated his family had no knowledge of these issues. The matter is under investigation. Superintendent of Police Rajesh Dwivedi said, A case of suicide by an elderly man has come to light. The suicide note is being examined. The post-mortem has been conducted, and the family has not made any allegations against anyone.

stories.title: BJP Yuva Morcha aspirants in UP may lose ground:Party’s proposed age cap could sideline most contenders as most leaders cross 35-yr limit
stories.summary: The age issue has become a sticking point among contenders for the state president position in Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha. The party is preparing to hand over the command of Yuva Morcha only to youth between 32 to 35 years of age. In such a situation, the candidacy of leaders for the UP Yuva Morcha president post could land in crisis. BJP's new national president Nitin Nabin is the youngest national president. The party's national president is just 45 years old, so there is ongoing discussion in the organization to also set the age limit of Yuva Morcha's national president between 32 to 35 years. The current president of Yuva Morcha in UP, Pranshudutt Dwivedi, is 43 years old. Pranshu has been the president of Yuva Morcha for about four and a half years. State President Pankaj Chaudhary has indicated the formation of advance fronts soon. More than a dozen young leaders in the state are claiming candidacy for the state president post of Yuva Morcha. However, not a single contender among the claimants falls within the age limit set by the party. All Front presidents will be changed Presidents of all seven frontal organizations of BJP will be changed. Youth Front President Pranshu Dutt Dwivedi has become MLC. Women's Front President Geeta Shakya is a Rajya Sabha member. OBC Front President Narendra Kashyap is Minister of State for Backward Classes Welfare (Independent Charge) in Yogi government. Narendra Kashyap has been working on both positions for four years, while the party has a one-person-one-post principle. SC Morcha President Ramchandra Kanaujia, Kisan Morcha State President Kameshwar Singh, Minority Morcha State President Kunwar Basil Ali and Scheduled Tribes Morcha President Sanjay Gond have not gotten the opportunity for adjustment in the government. All state presidents of the frontal organizations were appointed by then state president Swatantra Dev Singh in June 2021. No new team was formed in the frontal organizations during the tenure of outgoing state president Bhupendra Chaudhary. Therefore, a new team is set to be formed during Pankaj Chaudhary's tenure. State president too should be young one Political analyst Anand Rai believes that the president of the Youth Morcha should be young. In UP, Akhilesh Yadav became CM at the age of 39, BSP supremo Mayawati also became CM at the age of 40. Even earlier, leaders of age 35 have served as presidents in the Youth Morcha. Age should be more than 35 years Senior journalist Ratanmanilal says that stundent's education continues till the age of 25. Until the age of 30, one cannot gain social and political experience to work with political acumen. Youth Morcha is a major wing working among young people. Youth Morcha party workers go on to become office bearers in the main organization. The state president of Youth Morcha is also the face of the party. West weakened While Purvanchal's dominance has increased in government and organization, Western UP has weakened and Awadh is the weakest. If regional balance is not maintained in time with BJP's frontal organizations and state team formation along with Yogi government's cabinet expansion, BJP may have to face losses in assembly elections. Strong Claims from Brahmins and Thakurs The issue of Brahmin discontent is heated in the state. Political analysts believe that Brahmins don't hold many important positions in organization, government and administration. In such situation, Brahmins are considered the strongest contenders for the youth wing president post. Meanwhile, the UGC issue also continues to be a cause of concern for BJP. The UGC is being most strongly opposed by Brahmins, Thakurs, Kayasthas, Vaishyas, and Bhumihars. In this situation, Thakur leaders also have strong claims for the position of Youth Front President. Contenders and their age There are more than fifteen contenders for the state president position of the Youth Front. The contenders include Youth Front's national officials, state officials, and regional presidents. Among these, only two to three contenders fall within the age range of 32 to 35 years. Most contenders are 40 years and above in age. .

stories.title: The inside story of Shankaracharya’s sudden Magh Mela exit:Closed-door meeting held hours earlier, administration says, 'We expressed regret, but he insisted on apology'
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati's conflict with the Prayagraj administration lasted for 11 days and on the morning of January 28, Shankaracharya suddenly left the Magh Mela. This sudden turn of events surprised everyone. Dainik Bhaskar's investigation revealed that on the evening of January 27, a secret meeting was held by the administration to resolve the dispute. In this high-level meeting, agreement was reached on 3 important points. However, talks stalled on 2 points. First- The administration refused to give anything in writing. Second- Officials did not agree to make a public apology. The discussions from this meeting were conveyed to Shankaracharya that night. Since the administration was accepting their mistake in the whole matter, Shankaracharya decided to leave the Mela and announced this on the morning of January 28. Where did this meeting take place? Who all attended? What discussions happened between them? To understand this in detail, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Shankaracharya's disciple and officials from the Prayagraj administration. Read the report... See in 2 photos the scenes of Shankaracharya leaving Magh Mela and removal of the ashram- Officials seated in Dharma Sangh camp, Sridhranand becomes Shankaracharya's representative According to Shankaracharya's disciple Yogiraj, the administration arranged a high-level meeting to resolve the snan dispute that started from Mauni Amavasya. On the evening of January 27, officials reached the Dharma Sangh camp, which is located at some distance from Shankaracharya's camp on Triveni Marg. Magh Mela administration's Mela Officer Rishi Raj, Additional Mela Officer Dayanand Prasad and other officials of the Mela administration were present in the meeting. However, Shankaracharya's disciples did not attend this meeting. Instead, Mahant Shridharanand Brahmachari of Mankameshwar Temple in Prayagraj was sent to speak on behalf of Shankaracharya. According to Yogiraj, in this meeting, the administration presented its position on 3 issues. (All these points were accepted by Mahant Shridharanand.) Officials said - No apology, we will express regret Yogiraj explained - The Mela administration acknowledged that they made a mistake. They cited crowd control as the reason behind it. In these circumstances, Shankaracharya could not take the holy bath. Officials said - We regret this. Then Mahant Shridharanand said - Shankaracharya wants you to apologize. Regarding this, the officials said that we cannot make a public apology. But we can express regret. Officials said - You can take holy dip whenever you want, we will make all arrangements. This matter should now come to an end. Yogiraj said - When officials were asked to give these things in writing, they said it would not be possible. Now they are in front of you, saying everything, expressing regret. After this, the Mahant insisted why should Shankaracharya forgive you without written consent. Disciples say - On our behalf, the Mahant said that what happened at Sangam Nose on Mauni Amavasya day is only worthy of an apology. However, the administration wanted to limit it to just expressing regret. Therefore, no consensus could be reached until late night. Sources say - The Magh Mela is to continue till February 15, and people doing Kalpvas have also started returning. The main snan rituals are also complete, so Shankaracharya decided that since officials have already started accepting their mistake, they can now depart from the Magh Mela area. Before leaving the fair area, Shankaracharya held a press conference and said - Today my heart is very distressed. We are leaving without taking a bath. Don't know which leader will come, which party will come to compensate for this sorrow. Prayagraj has always been a land of faith and peace. I came here with devotion, but such an incident happened which I never expected. Those who have insulted Sanatani symbols will have to be shown their place. He said- "Yesterday I received a letter and proposal from the Magh Mela administration. It stated that I would be taken to Sangam in a palanquin with full respect for bathing. Flowers would be showered on me, but I rejected the proposal. When there is pain and anger in the heart, even holy water cannot give peace." Avimukteshwaranand said - If I had accepted the administration's words, then what about the incident of misbehavior and assault with Batuk and disciples? Therefore, it is appropriate for me to leave the fair area now. An attempt was made to understand the fair administration's side in this entire matter. However, even after several attempts, the fair officer did not receive the call. Now understand the entire controversy in 5 points

stories.title: Raj Chauhan murder case accused killed in Agra:Early morning encounters at 3 locations; 2 history-sheeter shot in leg
stories.summary: Arbaaz Khan alias Mansoori, an accused in the Raj Chauhan murder case, was gunned down in a late-night police encounter in Agra on Wednesday. The incident occurred when Arbaaz allegedly snatched a sub-inspector’s service pistol and opened fire while attempting to escape during a weapon recovery operation. Pistol snatched, firing during escape According to a statement issued by the police, Arbaaz had been taken to recover the country-made pistol used in the Raj Chauhan murder. Around 2 am, near Kanshiram Awas in the Tedi Bagiya area, he allegedly pushed a sub-inspector, grabbed his government-issued pistol, and tried to flee. While running, Arbaaz reportedly opened fire on the police team. Constable Manoj Kumar and Sub-Inspector Rishi sustained gunshot injuries. Bullets also struck the bulletproof jackets of Sub-Inspector Harendra Kumar and Inspector Bhanu Pratap, one round hitting each vest. Police retaliation and death Police fired back in self-defence. Arbaaz was hit by two bullets—one in the left side of the chest and another in his right leg. He was rushed to SN Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. The injured policemen were admitted to Agra District Hospital and are undergoing treatment. Official statement DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, In the Raj Chauhan murder case, five teams were initially formed and later four more teams were deployed. Suspects were identified and one accused, Arbaaz, was arrested. After his arrest, he was taken for recovery of the weapon. There, he snatched a pistol from our sub-inspector and opened fire, injuring two policemen. In self-defence, the police retaliated, in which he was shot. Background: Raj Chauhan murder case Raj Chauhan was shot dead on January 23 at the SN Guest House in the Tedi Bagiya area. He was riddled with bullets inside the guest house. Police recovered five empty cartridges from the spot. Investigations revealed that Raj was killed a day before his birthday by youths who had come with him. According to police, Raj’s associates tipped off the attackers. Five people were initially taken into custody, and during questioning, the names of Shoaib Mansoori and his accomplices surfaced. Arbaaz, a resident of Khandoli, was later arrested in connection with the murder. Raj’s mother, Neeru Chauhan, alleged that her son was murdered due to an old rivalry. She said that on Friday evening around 4 pm, four unknown youths came to their house, spoke to Raj for a long time, and then took him along. “We had never seen those boys before,” she said. Two more criminals shot in separate encounters Apart from Arbaaz, police also carried out encounters with two wanted criminals carrying rewards of ₹25,000 each on Wednesday night. Both were shot in the leg and arrested. They are currently undergoing treatment in hospital. The first encounter took place near the Dauki–Nadota underpass. Ashu Tiwari, son of Ravindra Tiwari and a resident of New Gaushala Ramganj in Etawah, opened fire at the police. In retaliation, he was shot in the leg. Police recovered an illegal country-made pistol, one live cartridge, one empty shell, and a .315 bore weapon from him. The second encounter occurred in the Trans-Yamuna area during night checking, following a tip-off. Accused Mohit Pandit, currently residing in Kalindi Vihar and originally from Etah, was injured by a bullet in the leg during the exchange of fire. An illegal pistol, one live cartridge, one empty shell, and a Splendor motorcycle were recovered from his possession. Police said investigations in the Raj Chauhan murder case and related criminal networks are ongoing.
