stories.title: Alankar Agnihotri reaches Kanpur home after quitting, mother welcomes:Bareilly City Magistrate says his fight is against Central Govt; supporters compare him with lion
stories.summary: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, who resigned in protest against the insult to Swami Avimukteshwaranand, returned home to Kanpur on Saturday. At his Keshav Nagar residence, women welcomed him with conch shells (shankh), while his mother, Geeta Agnihotri, garlanded and embraced him. Supporters also showered Alankar Agnihotri with flowers and garlands, chanting slogans like, ‘Look, the lion has come,’ and danced enthusiastically. Alankar accepted the greetings and told Dainik Bhaskar that he plans to meet Shankaracharya in two to three days and currently has no intention of accepting any position offered by him. He said, Our next step is the repeal of another black law of the country, the SC-ST Act. 95% of complaints filed are fake. People from general categories like Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Kayasthas, Vaishyas, Bhumihars, and OBC categories are harassed. Money is extorted. If the government does not take a decision on this by calling a special parliamentary session within 7 days, we will march towards Delhi with a movement. Alankar Agnihotri said, UGC Regulation 2026 was issued in the Gazette of the Government of India. I would now like to clearly name them, this is a well-planned, well-thought-out conspiracy by Modi and Shah. They got such a gazette prepared, which could make General and OBC fight among themselves.A conspiracy was hatched to influence the UP assembly elections to be held in 2027. It was the blessing of Bajrangbali that our conscience awakened in time. It could be stopped by the order of the Supreme Court. All parties are in our contact On the question of being in contact with political parties, Alankar Agnihotri said - 'All political parties, Brahmin organisations, farmer organisations, and upper caste society, OBC organisations are in our contact. SC-ST organisations are also in our contact.' Alankar criticises central government’s ‘Loot’ Alankar targeted the central government, saying it resembles the East India Company looting in the past, now led by two 'West India Company' figures, whose CEO and MD will be sent to Gujarat by chartered plane. He added that Kanpur, city of Tatya Tope and Nana Saheb, witnessed Dandi March-like protests and punishments. Since this government came to power, it expects 1% commission from the state, while MPs and MLAs face pressure from sycophantic ED, CBI, and IT officers, with the West India Company demanding extortion in their own ways. Resigned on January 26 Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri had resigned from his post on Republic Day. He cited the new UGC law and the beating of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's disciples as the reasons. However, his resignation was not accepted. The government suspended him and initiated an inquiry. On the evening of January 26, around 7:30 PM, the City Magistrate reached DM Avinash Singh's residence to meet him. Upon coming out, the City Magistrate said- I was held hostage for 45 minutes at the DM's residence. A call came to the DM from Lucknow. It was said, while abusing, that Pandit has gone mad. Keep him hostage overnight. I had already informed the media. I was released at the SSP's behest. I have fled to save my life. The City Magistrate vacated his official residence. As he left, he said he was staying with his acquaintances in Bareilly today. He will sit with them and decide the future strategy. Resigned by writing a 5-page letter Alankar Agnihotri also wrote a 5-page letter in his resignation. In which he said- 'During the Prayagraj Magh Mela, the topknot of Shankaracharya's disciples was caught.' He wrote- Such an incident shakes any ordinary Brahmin from within. It seems that the administration and the current government are working against Brahmins and saints. Their honor is being toyed with. There is no one to speak for Brahmins. Alankar Agnihotri asked if there is a preparation for the genocide of Brahmins. Along with the ADM, three officers stayed at his residence for about an hour to persuade him before leaving. Leaders of several Brahmin organisations and SP-Congress workers also met him, while protests took place outside. A PCS officer since 2019 with 15th rank, Alankar had earlier come into the spotlight for displaying a picture of Lord Bajrangbali in his office, which led to a ruckus by Bhim Army and an altercation with officials.

stories.title: Man kills wife and surrenders at police station in Hardoi:Confesses that his wife wanted to live with her lover, so he killed her
stories.summary: A shocking incident has emerged from Hardoi district, where a man murdered his wife and then voluntarily surrendered at the police station. The accused told police that his wife wanted to live with her lover, which led him to kill her. He informed officers that her body was lying inside their home. The confession caused panic at the police station. Police immediately detained the man and took him to his house, where they found the woman’s body. The incident took place late on Friday night in the Behta Gokul police station area. According to the initial police investigation, the woman had eloped with her lover on 13 January. She was recovered by police six days later and handed back to her husband. At that time, she reportedly told the police that she wished to live with her husband. However, tensions continued at home after her return, eventually leading to the fatal incident. Marriage and family details The accused, Naveen Shukla (28), a resident of Raipur Gulariya, was married to Anju Shukla (25), who belonged to Surjipur village. The couple had been married for seven years. For the past five years, Naveen had been living with his wife at her parental home. Anju’s father, Suresh Pandey, had passed away and she had no brothers. She owned around 35 bighas of land, which Naveen managed. The couple had two young children. Alleged affair and elopement Naveen told the police that his wife was involved in an affair with a young man from the same village. He claimed that he repeatedly objected, but she did not stop seeing the man. On 13 January, Anju allegedly ran away with her lover. A complaint was lodged with the police the same day through the village head. On 19 January, police recovered Anju and questioned her about whom she wanted to live with. According to Naveen, she chose to return to him, and he brought her back home. Argument turns fatal Naveen said that initially, things appeared normal after Anju returned, but frequent arguments soon began. He alleged that she continued to meet her lover secretly. On Friday evening, another argument broke out between them. In a moment of rage, Naveen said he strangled his wife, leading to her death. Police action and custody At the time of the incident, Anju’s mother, Sukhrani, was sitting outside the house under a tin shed and was unaware of what was happening inside. After killing his wife, Naveen went straight to Behta Gokul police station and confessed to Station House Officer Dharmendra Giri. The SHO confirmed that Naveen has been taken into custody. A formal complaint is awaited, after which further legal action will be initiated. Mother demands strict punishment Anju’s mother, Sukhrani, said the family had no idea about the murder until Naveen surrendered. She stated that Naveen had been angry ever since her daughter returned home and that daily arguments had become common. She expressed concern for the couple’s two young children and demanded the strictest possible punishment for her son-in-law.

stories.title: Speeding truck crashes into two passenger autos in Agra:5 pilgrims returning from Char Dham killed, 8 injured
stories.summary: A speeding truck rammed into two passenger-loaded auto-rickshaws in Agra, killing five people on the spot. More than eight others were seriously injured. Following the crash, local people caught the truck driver and assaulted him. The collision was so severe that both auto-rickshaws were flung nearly 10 feet off the road, crashed into a tree and then overturned into a roadside ditch. Several passengers suffered serious head and facial injuries. One of the autos was completely wrecked and split into two parts, with its roof torn off. Passengers returning from Char Dham Yatra According to information, the auto-rickshaw passengers had returned from the Char Dham Yatra and were travelling from Agra railway station to their village. Eyewitnesses alleged that the truck driver was intoxicated and driving at a speed exceeding 100 kmph. 2 pictures of the accident- Truck lost control, crushed both autos Witnesses said the auto-rickshaws were moving along the side of the road when the speeding truck suddenly went out of control and ploughed into both vehicles, crushing them. Police rush to spot, injured admitted to hospital ADCP Aditya Kumar said information about the accident was received promptly and police teams reached the spot. All injured passengers were shifted to hospital for treatment. The accident occurred on Jalesar Road in the Khandauli police station area at around 11 am on Saturday.

stories.title: Avimukteshwaranand invited for Badrinath gate-opening ritual:Prayagraj Magh Mela administration had sought proof of his Shankaracharya status
stories.summary: Swami Avimukteshwaranand has been formally invited to participate, in his capacity as Shankaracharya, in the most important ritual held before the opening of the gates of Badrinath Dham in Uttarakhand. The invitation assumes significance as it has been extended at a time when a dispute is ongoing between the Shankaracharya and the Prayagraj Magh Mela administration. Earlier, the Magh Mela administration had sought documentary proof of Swami Avimukteshwaranand’s status as Shankaracharya. In response, he questioned the authority of the administration, subsequently left the Mela, and travelled to Kashi. On Friday, addressing the controversy, he demanded that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath provide proof of being a Hindu, giving the government a deadline of 40 days. Invitation issued on January 25 Pandit Ashutosh Dimri, President of the Shri Badrinath Dimri Dharmik Kendriya Panchayat, confirmed that the invitation was sent on January 25. Through this letter, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand has been requested to participate in the Gaadu Ghada Yatra, which travels from Rishikesh to Badrinath Dham. The Gaadu Ghada Yatra is a deeply rooted religious tradition that precedes the opening of the gates of Badrinath Dham. With the commencement of this yatra, the Char Dham Yatra is formally considered to have begun. What is the Gaadu Ghada Yatra? The Gaadu Ghada Yatra begins at the Royal Palace of Narendra Nagar in Tehri. As part of this sacred ritual, married women from the Dimri community observe a fast and prepare sesame oil using entirely traditional methods. No mechanical devices are used during the oil extraction process. To maintain ritual purity, the women cover their mouths with a yellow cloth while extracting the oil. The process involves the use of grinding stones (silbatta), mortars (okhli), and manual effort. Once prepared, the oil is poured into a silver urn known as the Gaadu Ghada. Under the leadership of the Dimri priest community, this urn is placed on a decorated chariot. The yatra then proceeds through several designated halts before reaching Badrinath Dham. On the day the temple gates open, Lord Badri Vishal is anointed with this sacred oil, marking the formal commencement of the Char Dham Yatra. Dates announced for Badrinath Dham opening Pandit Ashutosh Dimri informed that the gates of Badrinath Dham will open for devotees on April 23 at 6:15 am. This date was traditionally announced at the Royal Palace of Narendra Nagar on the occasion of Basant Panchami. The sesame oil will be prepared on April 7 at the Narendra Nagar palace through ritualistic procedures. The same evening, the Gaadu Ghada will depart from the Tehri royal court. On April 8, it will reach the guest house of the Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC) in Rishikesh, where it will be kept for public viewing by devotees. About the inviting organisation The Shri Badrinath Dimri Dharmik Kendriya Panchayat is a prominent religious body of the Dimri priest community associated with Badrinath Dham. It consists of Brahmin priests from Dimmar village and collectively takes decisions related to religious customs, temple rituals, the opening of the temple gates, the Tel Kalash (oil urn) procession, and worship practices. Who are the Dimri Brahmins? Roots linked to Adi Guru Shankaracharya Dimri Brahmins trace their origins to the tradition established by Adi Guru Shankaracharya. It is believed that when he founded the Char Dhams, he instituted a system under which priests from South India would serve in northern temples, while priests from North India would serve in southern temples. Under this tradition, the chief priests of Badrinath Dham are Namboodiri Brahmins from Kerala, known as Rawals. Settlement in Garhwal Dimri Brahmins are considered Dravidian Brahmins who migrated from Karnataka to Garhwal as assistant priests accompanying Adi Guru Shankaracharya. Over time, they settled permanently in Dimmar village, located in Patti Tali Chandpur near Karnaprayag in Chamoli district. The community came to be known as Dimri after the village. Continuing role in Badrinath traditions Even today, Dimri Brahmins play a crucial role in preserving the ancient traditions of Lord Badrinarayan. The initiation of the Gaadu Ghada Yatra before the opening of the temple gates is exclusively carried out by Dimri Baridars. The right to offer Bhog (food offerings) to the deity is also reserved for Dimri Pandits. Most major religious rituals of Badrinath Dham continue to be conducted under the guidance of the Dimri Panchayat.

stories.title: Meerut incident victim breaks silence, promises to take revenge:Says, 'Mother murdered in front of me', denies love angle, reveals kidnapping story
stories.summary: Ruby, the survivor of the Kapsad incident in Meerut, has strongly rejected claims of a love relationship with accused Paras, alleging that he stalked her, murdered her mother in front of her eyes, and abducted her at gunpoint. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the traumatised girl said, Paras ruined my life and my home. Either the government should hang him, or if the law cannot punish him, then I myself will avenge my mother’s murder. Holding her mother's photo, Ruby breaks down crying. She just keeps saying- Paras has snatched my most precious thing from me. He has destroyed everything I had. I never loved him. But now I certainly hate him. Dainik Bhaskar heard the complete detailed story of her mother's murder and her kidnapping from Ruby for the first time on January 8. Story of Kidnapping and Murder Paras studied in my school, I was in 12th, he was a 9th grade student Ruby said she passed Class 12 in 2022, while Paras was a Class 9 student in the same school. “I didn’t even know him personally. I only knew that he used to follow me and insist on friendship. He lived about one to one-and-a-half kilometres from my house and would often stand in my lane. I never spoke to him,” she said. My ID was hacked and obscene videos were shared She alleged that Paras repeatedly sent her Instagram requests. When she did not accept them, he hacked her social media account and posted obscene videos. “I came to know only when my relatives asked me about those posts,” she said. She informed her brother, who took her to Paras’s house. However, Paras denied the allegations in front of everyone, leading to a heated argument. “My brother brought me back home and scolded me. Getting my hacked ID fixed became a compulsion. I lied to Paras, saying I liked him and asked him to restore my account. Later, my family took away my phone and got the ID deactivated,” Ruby said. She emphasised that claims describing Paras as her boyfriend are false. Paras attacked mother in 2024 Ruby alleged that in 2024, Paras forcibly entered their house and attacked her mother, Sunita, causing serious injuries. Following this incident, a village panchayat was held. “There was nothing in that panchayat that brought shame to my family because of me,” she said. Wrote a letter asking Paras to spare me... Ruby further says - After all this happened, my family arranged my marriage. But Paras still kept pursuing me. This happened about 3 to 4 months ago. That's when I wrote my first and last letter to Paras. After these incidents, Ruby’s family fixed her marriage. Despite this, she claimed Paras continued to pursue her. Around three to four months before the incident, she wrote him a letter—her first and last communication—asking him to leave her alone. “I told him my marriage was fixed and that I could not leave my family. I asked him to stop following me,” she said, adding that the letter was delivered through a friend from the same village. Now know about the story of January 8 Paras grabbed my hand and dragged me Recounting the events of January 8, Ruby said her father had gone to the fields early in the morning. Around 8 am, she was walking to the fields with her mother and two friends when Paras suddenly appeared near the sugarcane fields, partially covered with a shawl. “He grabbed my hand and started dragging me. I screamed and begged him to leave me, but he didn’t,” she said. Mom came to save but was struck with axe When her mother rushed to intervene, Paras allegedly attacked her twice with an axe, striking her on the face and head. “My mother collapsed, bleeding heavily. Even then, Paras kept holding my hand,” Ruby said. She alleged that Paras threatened to kill her, her three brothers, and her father if she did not go with him. “He kept the axe on my neck. My two friends ran back to the village. I don’t know if my mother was alive then. I only know she was bleeding,” she said. I jumped into the small canal to save myself Ruby said she attempted to escape by jumping into a small canal, but Paras followed her and caught her. “He placed the axe over me. I was too scared to scream or ask for help,” she said. She claimed Paras was accompanied by two other men, one of whom she believes was named Sunil, who allegedly supplied the axe used in the attack. Paras took me to Delhi then Haridwar Paras then took her away from the village in a vehicle. The pair spent the night behind a hotel before travelling in a truck the next day. “The truck driver had consumed alcohol. I wanted to ask for help, but I was scared Paras would kill him too,” she said. Ruby said Paras took her to Delhi and then to Haridwar. They later boarded trains, moving from place to place. I didn't know what was happening at home Ruby said she had no contact with her family during this period and did not know what was happening at home. Neither she nor Paras had a phone. On January 10, she said she pretended to agree to marry Paras to gain his trust. “I told him I loved him and would marry him, but asked him to let me speak to my family once,” she said. Paras then used a passenger’s phone on a train to call his friend, Dr Rajendra. That call enabled the police to trace their location. “The police reached and caught us,” she said. From January 8 to January 10, she said they kept travelling by train while Paras repeatedly threatened to kill her. “I was forced to say I would marry him. Only then did he agree,” she said. Paras is psychotic, he would kill everyone Describing the accused as mentally unstable, Ruby said Paras had earlier attacked his grandfather and had previously assaulted her mother. “This time, he killed my mother in front of me. I genuinely believed he would kill me, my brothers, and my father. That fear forced me to stay with him,” she said. She also said two village girls were eyewitnesses to the incident. “They were with me on January 8 and saw Paras killing my mother with an axe,” she said. Ruby again denied any romantic relationship. “There was no love, no friendship, no relationship, and no marriage. Even during the kidnapping, nothing happened between us,” she said, countering arguments raised about her appearance. “If I had willingly run away, I would have taken clothes, money, a phone, or documents. I had nothing. I was empty-handed.” 2 village girls are eyewitnesses to the incident Ruby said she learnt of her mother’s death only on January 11, after being brought back to Meerut by police. “My mother died on January 8 itself when Paras attacked her. I didn’t even get to see her face one last time,” she said. She concluded by reiterating her demand for justice. “Paras knew my mother was the most precious person in my life. He took her away from me. I want justice, and that justice will come only when Paras is hanged,” she said. Ruby said she has maintained the same statement before police, in court, and during every inquiry. “This is my truth, and I will never go back on it,” she said. stories.title: Gangrape victim dies after consuming poison in Meerut:Brother refuses last rites until minister visits; police arrest main accused and continue probe
stories.summary: In Meerut, following the gangrape, the victim consumed pesticide and ended her life. After family protests, the police conducted the post-mortem of the minor late Friday night in a hurry. The body was then sent to the village under police force. The victim’s brother said—“The police were pressuring us to conduct the last rites at night. But we will not perform the cremation until Minister Narendra Kashyap comes to meet us.” It is reported that the boyfriend lured the girl home on the night of 24 January. There, along with two friends, he held her captive and committed the act. When the girl lost consciousness, the accused fled. The next morning, 25 January, at around 5 a.m., the boyfriend’s mother entered the room and found the girl lying unconscious, covered in blood. With the help of neighbors, the mother brought the girl to her home. After two hours, she regained consciousness. When her family inquired about the incident, she remained silent. Later, she went to her room and consumed poison. Based on the family’s complaint, the police have registered a case. The main accused has been arrested, while the search for the other two accused continues. However, the police have described the case as an affair. Girl's brother said - My sister was covered in blood The victim's brother said - “On January 25th morning when we woke up, sister was not at home. We started searching. We were inquiring with people in the neighborhood. During this time, Anuj's mother from the neighborhood brought my sister home in an unconscious state. At that time my sister's clothes were soaked in blood. When her condition deteriorated, we laid her down there.” The victim's brother said - “After regaining consciousness, I asked my sister and she told me that Anuj and his friends raped me. After this, I consoled her and she went to rest in the room. Meanwhile, my sister consumed pesticide kept in the house. We immediately rushed her to a private hospital in Mawana, from where doctors referred her to medical for treatment.” Doctor said - Girl was admitted on January 26 Dr. Arvind, Head of Medicine Department at Medical Hospital said - “The patient was admitted to the medical college in serious condition on the morning of January 26. The patient was on ventilator since admission. In between, slight improvement was also seen in her condition, but from Thursday morning the situation started deteriorating again. During treatment, the patient passed away on Friday evening.” SSP said - Young man was arrested and sent to jail Meerut SSP Dr. Vipin Tada said - “A girl from Bahsuma police station area was having an affair with a boy from her neighborhood. Both were meeting regularly. Based on the family's complaint, action was taken and a young man from the village was arrested and sent to jail. Additionally, other people named by the victim's family are also being taken into custody.”

stories.title: Wife murdered by strangulation in Gurugram:Husband absconding, calls brother-in-law saying he beat her; police register case and begin search
stories.summary: In Gurugram, Haryana, a husband allegedly strangled his wife to death. After the incident, he reportedly called his brother-in-law and said he had beaten his wife. “She is injured, take her,” he told him. When the woman’s family arrived, they found her body lying on the bed. Her husband was missing at the time, and the police were informed immediately. The family alleged that Sunny often suspected his wife’s character, which frequently led to arguments and physical abuse. Based on a complaint lodged by the deceased’s brother, the Sector 37 police registered a case under multiple sections against Sunny, and a manhunt is currently underway. Now learn about the entire matter in sequence... 2 children after marriage The deceased has been identified as Sheelu (30), a resident of Khas Bhara village, Auraiya district, Uttar Pradesh. Sheelu’s brother, Alok, said that she married Sunny Dayal, a resident of Rani Ghat Colony, Kanpur, eight years ago. The couple had two children—a 7-year-old son and a 3-year-old daughter. Living in Gurugram for 4 years Alok said that Sheelu and Sunny had been living with their children in a rented house in Khandasa, Gurugram, for the past four years. Both worked as laborers. He added that Sunny often doubted Sheelu’s character, which frequently led to disputes and abuse. Informed by phone after 12 hours Alok further said that late on 28 January, Sunny strangled Sheelu to death. Approximately 12 hours later, at around 3 pm on 29 January, Sunny called and claimed there had been a fight in which Sheelu was injured, asking the family to come and take her. Alok informed his sister Neeraj about the call. Dead body was lying on the bed Neeraj’s husband, Ravi, sent Sheelu’s other brother, Kapil, who works in a company in Sector 37, to her room. Kapil found Sheelu’s dead body lying on the bed. Their two children were at home, while Sunny was absconding. The family then informed the police. SHO says - searching for the accused SHO Manjit of Sector 37 police station said that the incident was reported to the police on the evening of 29 January. A team reached the scene and a forensic team was called for investigation. The post-mortem of the deceased will be conducted tomorrow. Sunny remains absconding, and the police have registered a case against him and begun a search.

stories.title: UP Police draw criticism for ‘half-encounters’:Allahabad High Court warns officers, issues 6-point guidelines against unlawful actions for awards
stories.summary: Allahabad High Court has expressed strong concern over UP Police using ‘half-encounter’ methods. The court observed that officers are firing guns unnecessarily just to gain praise, early promotions, and social media recognition. The bench of Justice Arun Kumar Deshwal has issued 6-point strict guidelines. The court warned that if police fail to follow Supreme Court norms in encounter cases, the district SP, SSP, and Police Commissioner will be personally held guilty of contempt. Court said - Punishing accused is not police's job The High Court said - Only the judiciary has the right to punish the accused, not the police. India is a democratic country and here the law runs according to the Constitution, not based on personal thinking. The court also noted that in some cases, officers deliberately shoot the accused below the knees so that incidents can be reported as ‘half-encounters’ to claim bravery. “This method is completely unacceptable under the law,” the court said. Order came during hearing of bail petition The strict order was issued on Friday while hearing a bail petition. The accused had suffered serious injuries in a police encounter. The court noted that no police officer was injured, raising questions about the necessity and proportionality of using weapons. The court directed strict compliance with Supreme Court guidelines, emphasizing the PUCL (People’s Union for Civil Liberties) vs Maharashtra State (2014) ruling. Despite this, UP Police have repeatedly ignored these rules. “The police cannot take the law into their own hands for praise or awards,” the court said clearly. High Court's 6 Strict Guidelines 1- FIR and Investigation 2- Names in FIR 3- Medical and Statement 4- Report to Court 5- Ban on Promotion and Awards Victim's Family Has Right to Complain Court's Clear Message Now look at the encounter statistics in UP… 259 criminals killed in encounters in 8 years From March 2017 to October 2025, UP Police killed 259 criminals in encounters. During this period, there were more than 15,000 encounters, 31,000 arrests, and over 10,000 people shot.

stories.title: Moid Khan acquitted in Ayodhya gangrape case:Son Zaheer insists demolished complex belongs to uncle, family plans to challenge bulldozer action
stories.summary: In Ayodhya, in the gangrape case, the court has acquitted Moid Khan. His servant Raju has been held responsible. The decision was based on the DNA report. Against this decision, the Uttar Pradesh government will now approach the High Court. It will challenge Moid’s acquittal. Moid is still in jail; another case under the Gangster Act is pending against him. Moid’s son, Zaheer Khan, is also preparing a strong defense in the High Court. There are two main reasons— After Moid’s acquittal, Dainik Bhaskar contacted his family to understand the difficulties they faced from being accused of rape to now being acquitted, and whether they feel their honor can be restored. About 20 km from Ayodhya, on Bharat Kund Road in Bhadersa, Moid Khan’s complex stood. It had 50 shops. Only 50 meters from this complex, there was a 3,000-square-meter bakery run by Moid Khan. This was the place where the alleged rape was said to have occurred. After the allegations, the police took two major actions. First, an FIR was filed against Moid and Raju. Second, the bakery and complex were demolished using a bulldozer. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited the spot where the bulldozer action occurred on August 3, 2024. Seeing the debris of the A-1 bakery shop, we met Moid’s son Zaheer Khan and began a QA session. Q: Who all are in your family, and what is the atmosphere after the court verdict? A: We are four brothers—me, Nadeem, Mafeesh, Javed. Except for Javed, the others are married. We have three sisters; all are married. Even after the court verdict, people still need to be convinced that our father did nothing. Eyes still question us today. Q: The victim’s family says Moid was protected by an SP MP; what do you say? A: We have never met MP Awadhesh Prasad. Whatever people are saying, if there’s any photo of me, they should show it. Q: After this case, did Akhilesh ever speak to you? A: Akhilesh is very big; no local leader even came to meet us. Q: The court has acquitted Moid Khan; what do you say? A: We will thank the court. The DNA report clarified everything. The court realized that a 72-year-old man is innocent. Q: The victim’s family says they feel threatened by Moid Khan. A: Only the aunt (victim’s mother) can say what kind of fear they have. Whether they are afraid of us or someone else… because we never did anything like this. Why she says so, she can explain. Q: Was this rape case politicized? A: Everyone knows how local leaders misinformed CM Yogi Adityanath. In the first FIR, my father’s name wasn’t there. In the second FIR, who put his name—was it a former councilor or the leader contesting the chairman election? My father had no role. Yes, it was the boy, and for that, we were prepared to face any punishment. Q: How was your father’s condition when the rape allegations arose? A: He kept crying; his mouth developed sores. He was extremely disturbed and stayed in high-security jail. It was his first criminal case imprisonment. Earlier, he was arrested during SP dharnas, but that was different. Whenever he met in jail, he said these people trapped us. Q: The bakery was demolished; will you rebuild it? A: We lived in Surat and started the bakery two years ago. Media showed lots of properties, but that wasn’t true. The administration received incorrect feedback. Our father was a social worker and city president; people respected what he said. Q: Was the bakery built on loan? How much loss? A: It cost ₹30–35 lakh. After the demolition, materials inside were stolen. No loan was taken; money came from relatives. We will not rebuild the bakery immediately. First, we will work elsewhere and then consider the bakery. The 50-shop complex’s plan was approved by Bhadersa Nagar Panchayat, and the family has the documents. Q: Did you face difficulties in court? A: Only our hearts can tell. How much we had to do, how we reached court after getting trapped in this case—it was our first time. Q: If UP government goes to High Court, what is the next step? A: What can a child do for her father? Whatever is possible, we will do. No one will support us. During bulldozer action, we shouted that the shopping complex was not our property, but the administration didn’t listen. It was our uncle’s property. Our A-1 bakery shop occupied only 3,000 sq ft and wasn’t our land. Raju's DNA also matched On July 29, 2024, a 12-year-old girl in Bhadersa, Ayodhya, filed a gangrape case. She was pregnant at the time. Moid Khan and his servant Raju Khan were made accused. The FIR was filed, and the next day Moid and Raju were arrested. Later, under court orders on August 7, 2024, the minor rape survivor underwent abortion at Queen Mary Hospital, Lucknow. The victim alleged that she worked with Raju Khan, who introduced her to Moid about two-and-a-half months earlier. She claimed in the complaint that Moid, along with Raju, raped her. A video was recorded to intimidate her. She was allegedly sexually exploited for around two-and-a-half months. Now, in court, Moid has been proven innocent, while his servant Raju was found involved. Raju’s DNA also matched the fetus’s DNA. UP Government Used Bulldozer Moid Khan’s shopping complex was demolished on August 22, 2024. The UP government conducted the bulldozer operation. At the time, the then District Magistrate of Ayodhya, Chandra Vijay Singh, said Moid Khan’s bakery was built illegally on pond land, so action was taken. CM Yogi Adityanath claimed in the Assembly that Moid, associated with SP, was part of an MP’s team and involved in the rape of a 12-year-old minor. After the FIR, CM met the victim’s family. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav then demanded DNA tests for Moid and Raju. Moid’s defense lawyer, Saeed Khan, told a media channel that the DNA test result was crucial in the acquittal. The court declared Moid innocent and acquitted him with honor. Speaking to media, Special Public Prosecutor Virendra Kumar said this decision will be challenged in the High Court. The case will continue to be pursued.

stories.title: How much damage will BJP face from Shikha insult:Party secured most Brahmin votes in last five elections, where will their anger shift now?
stories.summary: A series of recent incidents in Uttar Pradesh has triggered strong resentment within the Brahmin community, placing the BJP and the state government under mounting pressure. First, BJP Brahmin MLAs who had gathered to discuss social concerns within the community were issued notices for indiscipline. Soon after, at the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati was allegedly insulted, and his disciples were beaten after their topknots (shikha) were forcibly pulled. Both incidents have deeply angered the Brahmin community, which has traditionally been one of the BJP’s most loyal support bases. Given that Brahmins have voted overwhelmingly for the party in the past five elections, questions are now being raised about the political cost of this discontent and the options available to the community going forward. Why the Brahmin vote matters in UP ? Brahmins constitute around 9 to 11 per cent of Uttar Pradesh’s population. Their influence is particularly strong in 31 of the state’s 75 districts. In regions such as Purvanchal, Central UP and Bundelkhand, political observers often say that the party backed by Brahmins stands a strong chance of forming the government. Historically, Brahmins have functioned as a decisive swing vote. Their socio-economic influence, articulate leadership and ability to shape opinion among other castes have allowed them to play a key role in determining electoral outcomes. However, one defining feature of Brahmin politics has been their inability to remain permanently aligned with any single party. Brahmin support until 1980 In the decades following Independence, Brahmins largely remained loyal to the Congress party. Prominent Brahmin leaders such as Govind Ballabh Pant, Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna and Narayan Dutt Tiwari served as Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh. Brahmin support formed the backbone of Congress’s so-called “umbrella coalition”, which included Muslims, Dalits and other communities. This coalition helped Congress secure a landslide victory in the 1985 Assembly elections, winning 269 seats. However, disillusionment set in during the Ram Temple movement and following the implementation of the Mandal Commission. Shift towards BJP in the 1990s The Mandal Commission alienated Brahmins from the Janata Dal, while the firing on karsevaks in Ayodhya under Mulayam Singh Yadav further angered the community. The BJP capitalised on this unrest by uniting Hindu voters divided by Mandal politics and intensifying the Ram Temple movement. As a result, Brahmins aligned with the BJP in large numbers for the first time. This shift proved decisive in the 1991 Assembly elections, when the BJP won a full majority with 221 seats. BSP gains Brahmin support in 2007 In 2007, the Bahujan Samaj Party successfully wooed Brahmin voters with the slogan, “Haathi nahi Ganesh hai, Brahma Vishnu Mahesh hai.” Satish Mishra was appointed General Secretary, and prominent Brahmin leaders were inducted into the party. Brahmin conferences were organised across districts, leading to a mass shift away from the BJP. The BSP benefited significantly, forming a government with an absolute majority of 206 seats. SP attracts Brahmins in 2012 In the 2012 Assembly elections, Brahmins once again changed allegiance. Around 19 per cent supported the Samajwadi Party, helping it return to power with 224 seats. However, this alignment proved temporary, as the community gradually gravitated back towards the BJP. BJP dominance from 2014 to 2022 From 2014 onwards, Brahmins were almost fully mobilised in favour of the BJP. The party won 71 Lok Sabha seats in 2014 and maintained overwhelming Brahmin support in the 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024 elections. According to the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies (CSDS), 83 per cent of Brahmin voters backed the BJP in 2017, rising to 89 per cent in the 2022 Assembly elections. Signs of discontent in 2024 The 2024 Lok Sabha elections, however, marked the beginning of visible discontent. Although the BJP still secured 79 per cent of Brahmin votes, 16 per cent shifted towards the Mahagathbandhan (Grand Alliance). This change translated into electoral losses, with the alliance winning 43 seats while the BJP-led coalition was restricted to 37. Shankaracharya incident deepens resentment Anger intensified following the alleged insult to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and the assault on his disciples at the Magh Mela. Earlier, BJP Brahmin MLAs had met at P.N. Pathak’s residence to discuss community issues, but were served notices by the party. While the BJP was still attempting damage control, the Prayagraj incident further inflamed tensions. Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri resigned in protest but was suspended and subjected to an inquiry. In contrast, Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar faced no action after resigning in support of CM Yogi Adityanath, despite past allegations regarding his disability certificate. Senior journalist Triyugi Narayan Tiwari said these contrasting actions suggest systemic bias against Brahmins, further fuelling resentment. Growing silence within BJP Although many Brahmin leaders and MLAs within the BJP are reportedly distressed, fear of disciplinary action has prevented open dissent. Senior BJP leader and Rashtriya Parshuram Parishad founder Pandit Sunil Bharala acknowledged deep hurt within the community, stating that even Sanatan society feels humiliated. He added that the BJP may be under the illusion that Brahmins have nowhere else to go, whereas in reality, the community is actively exploring alternatives. What options lie ahead for 2027? Senior journalist Sharat Pradhan believes the resentment has been building for years and intensified by incidents such as the Vikas Dubey encounter and action against Harishankar Tiwari. For the first time, Brahmins feel they are being deliberately targeted. Looking ahead to 2027, the community appears inclined to support whichever party can effectively challenge the BJP. While the BJP dismisses claims of dissatisfaction, opposition parties, including SP, BSP and Congress, are actively courting Brahmin voters. Congress, seen as the community’s traditional political home, could play a decisive role if it contests the elections alongside the SP, potentially reshaping Uttar Pradesh’s political landscape.

stories.title: Dense fog alert issued in 30 UP districts:Rain likely from Feb 1 to 3 as temperatures drop sharply; Bulandshahr emerging as coldest location in state
stories.summary: Cold conditions have returned to Uttar Pradesh following recent rainfall. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for dense fog in 30 districts of the state. On Friday, temperatures dropped across most regions due to cold north-westerly winds. Visibility drops sharply in several cities Dense fog severely reduced morning visibility in many areas. Bareilly and Agra recorded zero visibility, while Aligarh and Najibabad reported visibility of around 50 metres. Bulandshahr emerged as the coldest district in the state on Friday. Cold winds from snow-covered hills Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that after the passage of the previous active western disturbance, cold and dry north-westerly winds blowing in from snow-covered hill regions caused a significant drop in temperatures over the past 48 hours. In several places, temperatures fell below normal levels. Pictures of Friday's Weather- Western disturbance to activate again With increasing atmospheric stability, dense fog is likely on January 31, which may lead to a further fall in temperatures. Due to the impact of another western disturbance, rain is expected across parts of Uttar Pradesh from February 1 to February 3. January rainfall 39% below normal January remained relatively dry in the state. According to Meteorological Department data, Lucknow recorded 8.6 mm of rainfall in January, compared to the normal 14.1 mm for the month—around 39 percent below average. Authorities have advised people to remain cautious during early morning travel due to poor visibility and changing weather conditions.

stories.title: Rain expected in UP in first week of February:Cold to intensify, western disturbance may lower temperatures across several districts
stories.summary: Cold conditions have returned to Uttar Pradesh in the closing days of January, surprising residents who believed winter was drawing to an end. Just as temperatures appeared to be easing, the weather took a sudden turn, with rain and hail reported from several parts of the state. Meteorologists now warn that similar conditions may prevail once again in early February. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), rainfall is likely in many districts of Uttar Pradesh between February 1 and February 3. The renewed spell of winter weather has raised questions about the reasons behind the sudden January rain and hail, how severe the cold has been this season, and what February may bring, particularly for agriculture. How has the weather been in UP so far? Mahesh Palawat, a weather expert with Noida-based Skymet Weather, explained that Uttar Pradesh has experienced comparatively milder winters than in the past two years. Both maximum and minimum temperatures in December and January remained above normal levels. In North India, the average winter maximum temperature typically ranges between 20°C and 22°C, while minimum temperatures usually fall between 10°C and 15°C. According to Palawat, both these averages were exceeded in Uttar Pradesh this season, meaning that extreme cold conditions were largely absent. This assessment is echoed by Mohammad Danish, a scientist at the Lucknow Meteorological Centre, who stated that the intensity of cold this winter was noticeably lower compared to last year. Why did rain and hail occur in January? Meteorologist Mohammad Danish attributed the unseasonal rain and hail to repeated Western Disturbances. A Western Disturbance is a weather system that originates in the Mediterranean region and West Asia and travels eastwards towards North India. During winter, these systems have a significant influence on northern weather patterns. In January, several Western Disturbances remained active one after another. Their impact increased moisture levels in the atmosphere, and the interaction between cold winds led to rainfall. In certain areas, clouds developed to considerable heights. This vertical cloud formation, combined with strong wind activity and sudden temperature contrasts between warm and cold air, resulted in hailstorms along with rain. Cold likely to intensify as new system becomes active According to Mahesh Palawat, a fresh Western Disturbance is expected to affect north-west India between January 31 and February 2. This system is likely to bring heavy rainfall and snowfall to the Himalayan region. As a result, colder air from the mountains will move into the plains, intensifying cold conditions across the Gangetic belt, including Uttar Pradesh. The activation of this system could also lead to a drop in temperatures and the development of cold wave conditions. Additionally, rain and snowfall may reduce visibility in some areas, potentially disrupting road and rail traffic. Rain likely in several districts of Western UP Mohammad Danish said that the impact of the Western Disturbance will once again alter weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh. Light to moderate rainfall is expected in several districts of western UP. In some locations, thunderstorms and hail may also occur. Eastern Uttar Pradesh, including cities such as Lucknow, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Prayagraj, is expected to experience a more pronounced impact during this spell. Wider impact across North and Central India Mahesh Palawat noted that the influence of the Western Disturbance will not be limited to Uttar Pradesh alone. Its effect will also be felt across other north-western plain states, including Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, western Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. These regions may witness light to heavy rainfall. In addition, parts of central India, such as Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and adjoining areas, are also likely to receive some rainfall during this period. Overall, while this winter has been milder than usual in Uttar Pradesh, the renewed activity of Western Disturbances suggests that cold, rain and weather fluctuations will continue to affect the state into early February, with implications for daily life, traffic and agriculture.

stories.summary: सिंधौली की सिंदूर फिजिकल एकेडमी में शहीद सरज सिंह की शहादत को याद करने के लिए एक भावपूर्ण श्रद्धांजलि कार्यक्रम आयोजित किया गया। इस कार्यक्रम की अध्यक्षता रिटायर्ड सेना जवान ठाकुर उमेश प्रताप सिंह ने की। शहीद की पत्नी ने भी नम आंखों से अपने पति को श्रद्धांजलि दी। सभी ने शहीदों को याद किया।

stories.title: इस बार निडर होकर आकलन करेंगी डीएलएड प्रशिक्षु, होगी सुरक्षा
stories.summary: देवरिया में परिषदीय विद्यालयों में कक्षा एक एवं दो के बच्चों का आकलन डीएलएड प्रशिक्षुओं द्वारा किया जाएगा। निपुण प्लस एप पर एसओएस बटन की सुविधा के साथ, प्रशिक्षु असुरक्षा की स्थिति में तुरंत सहायता प्राप्त कर सकेंगे। 75% सही उत्तर देने वाले बच्चे निपुण विद्यार्थी घोषित होंगे और विद्यालय भी निपुणता के मानक परखेंगे।

stories.title: नींव भरी जमीन पर कब्जे का आरोप, एसडीएम से शिकायत

stories.title: प्रथम बार मतदाता बने युवाओं का हुआ सम्मान, लोकतंत्र के पर्व में भाग लेने की अपील

stories.title: छात्राओं के बीच युवक ने दौड़ाया घोड़ा, मना करने पर शिक्षक को पीटा

stories.title: छात्रा ने जमा की पूरी फीस, फिर भी कॉलेज ने नहीं किया रेजिस्ट्रेशन, परीक्षा के समय हुआ खुलासा

stories.summary: नौचंदी थाना क्षेत्र में एक युवक को बेहोश कर लूटने के मामले में पुलिस ने मानव दीक्षित को गिरफ्तार किया है। पीड़ित आशु गोयल ने बताया कि लूट के दौरान उसकी दो सोने की अंगूठियां, चेन और पैसे चुराए गए थे। व्यापारियों ने पुलिस की कार्यशैली पर सवाल उठाते हुए थाने में हंगामा किया।

stories.title: UP Metro sets target of developed India by 2047:Celebrations at depots and stations on Republic Day; future plans shared
stories.summary: When the heartbeat of the city, the Kanpur Metro, starts dancing to the rhythm of patriotism, you know the scene is something special. On the glorious occasion of the 77th Republic Day, such a flood of enthusiasm swept through Kanpur Metro Depot and stations that every heart called out 'Jai Hind'. Resolution and high aspirations for developed India The ceremony began at the Metro Depot located at Gurudev Chauraha, where UPMRC Project Director Arvind Meena hoisted the tricolor and gave the salute. Meanwhile, Managing Director Sushil Kumar conducted the flag hoisting in Lucknow and administered the oath of 'Developed India' to everyone. MD Sushil Kumar shared an enthusiastic vision, stating that Uttar Pradesh's metro network is now unstoppable. He said, "UPMRC has a crucial role in making India a developed nation by 2047. Today, we are at the third position in the metro network globally and will soon be at the second position." 'Blood of Patriotism' flows at Motijheel The true meaning of the Republic is service to society. Exemplifying this, a massive blood donation camp was organized at Motijheel Metro Station. Citizens and metro staff participated enthusiastically in this camp, organized in collaboration with Sankalp Seva Samiti, Big FM, and IIT Kanpur. Future 'Metro Map' will drive progress in UP: The future picture presented by UPMRC is nothing less than a golden dream. Almost every major city in the state will get the speed of the metro: Kanpur: 200 km proposed network. Lucknow: Expansion up to 225 km. Agra, Varanasi, Prayagraj, and Noida: Hundreds of km of new network. Ayodhya, Mathura, and Jhansi: Metro will also make its presence on 50-50 km tracks here. Number 1 in efficiency, UP Metro on track for profits It should be noted that UPMRC has also set benchmarks in management. In tier-2 cities like Kanpur and Agra, the metro is not only safe and punctual, but is also setting national standards with minimum costs and maximum revenue. In terms of operational efficiency, it is competing with some of the world's best systems.

stories.title: Student commits suicide after mother scolds him for flying kites:Boy scolded in front of friends, body found hanging on second floor in Meerut
stories.summary: A Class-9 student died by suicide in Meerut after being scolded by his mother for flying kites. The boy had been flying kites for the past three days, following which his mother reprimanded him in front of his friends. Distressed by this, the student went to his room on the second floor of the house around 11 am on Monday. When his friends went to check on him at around 12:30 pm, they found him hanging. Police reached the spot after being informed and sent the body for a post-mortem. The incident took place in Sector-3 of Shastri Nagar under the Nauchandi police station area. Anant Chauhan (14), a Class 9 student of Vidya Mandir School, was the son of Vinay Chauhan, who works as a driver. According to the family, Anant had been flying kites continuously for the past two days. Even on Basant Panchami, despite the rainfall, he went to the rooftop to fly kites. On January 26, a holiday, Anant again went to the roof with his friends early in the morning to fly kites. Around 11 am, his mother scolded him in front of his friends, asking him to stop flying kites and focus on his studies. She told him that he had been flying kites for the last three days. Anant reportedly became upset after being reprimanded publicly. Family refused to conduct postmortem Anant became very angry with his mother. After this, he went to his room on the second floor of the house. He did not come out of the room for one and a half hours. Around 12:30, Anant's friends, after flying kites, came down from the roof and searched for him in his room. They saw Anant's body hanging from a noose. He had made a noose from a dupatta. After this, friends raised an alarm. They called Anant's parents by shouting. In a hurry, when family members came to his room, they fainted upon seeing their son's body. Police arrived on information, and family members took him to Popular Hospital after bringing him down. The doctors declared him dead. Police also questioned family members and neighbors about the incident. The family members refused to conduct a post-mortem. After this, the police handed over the body to them.

stories.title: Padma Shri awarded to 3 personalities from Lucknow:Anil Rastogi worked in 75 films; Thakral Ayurveda expert, Rajendra medicine specialist
stories.summary: Two renowned doctors from Lucknow and one theater artist will be honored with Padma Shri for their excellent services. These include well-known respiratory and TB specialists and former HOD of KGMU, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and former principal of Government Ayurvedic College, Tudiyaganj, Dr. Kewal Krishna Thakral. Additionally, CDRI scientist and famous theater artist, film actor Dr. Anil Rastogi's name has also been announced. The central government announced the names of Padma award recipients on the eve of Republic Day. Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who has been selected for the Padma Shri award, is also known as the father of KGMU's Pulmonary Medicine department. He has served from student to HOD in KGMU's Pulmonary Medicine department. Dainik Bhaskar had special conversations with all three personalities. Read the report... Read what Dr. Rajendra Prasad said... Dr. Rajendra Prasad said that as soon as the name was announced, people started calling. It's a big day, a big moment. Today I would like to thank all those people who supported me in this journey. Feeling proud to receive this honor. Born in Basti, served patients in Lucknow Dr. Rajendra was born in 1950 in Mundera town of Basti. After completing his early education from Mundera, he did his high school from Khalilabad and intermediate from Christian College, Lucknow. In 1970, he got admission in MBBS at KGMU. After this, he completed his MD from the same institution. In 1984, he joined KGMU as a teacher. Later, he became the Head of the Department of Respiratory Medicine here. Achieved Success with Family's Support Dr. Rajendra Prasad shared that his late father, Gopichand, was a cloth merchant, and his late mother, Vijay Lakshmi, was a housewife. His son, Dr. Nikhit Gupta, is a teacher in the Medicine department at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute. His daughter, Dr. Pallavi, is a dentist and is married. He credited his wife, Meera Gupta, and family for helping him reach this far. Read what Dr. Thakral said about the honor... Father's inspiration led to becoming an Ayurvedic doctor Dr. Kewal Krishna Thakral, former principal of Government Ayurvedic College Tudiyaganj, expressed happiness on being selected for the Padma Shri award. He shared that besides his father, three brothers are also doctors. He became an Ayurvedic doctor inspired by them. Dr. Thakral said that he took admission in BAMS in 1964 at the Government Ayurvedic College, Tudiyaganj. Dr. KK Thakral, who lives in E Block of Rajajipuram, shared that he journeyed from lecturer to principal and director in Ayurvedic colleges. He retired in 1996. He presented 66 research papers, of which 54 were published in India and 12 abroad. He wrote several books, including the principles of Shalya Tantra. His book on Kshara Sutra surgery expertise was published in English. Received many Honors Dr. Thakral has received many honors like Ayurveda Ratnakar Award in 1991, the Ayurveda Brihaspati Award in 1992, National Herbal Conservation Award in 2010. He has also received the National Ayurveda Vidyapeeth, New Delhi, 2001 Fellowship. Now learn about theater artist Dr. Anil Rastogi... Dr. Rastogi is simple, natural, and accessible 83 years of age, around a thousand stage performances as an actor in a hundred plays, more than 75 films, and acting in more than 14 web series and TV serials. Despite so many achievements, it's not easy to remain simple, natural and accessible. Dr. Anil Rastogi loves Lucknow dearly, and Lucknow is equally fond of him. When the news of his receiving the Padma Shri honor came, the city residents were overjoyed. Gave credit for success to wife Anil, who was a scientist at CDRI, remained associated with Darpan Theatre Group. He said that along with the love of audiences, the government has also honored my work, which is a matter of great joy. My wife, Sudha Rastogi, has made a big contribution to my journey so far. Dr. Anil Rastogi has received Yash Bharati-2017, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2023, Pataliputra Lifetime Achievement Award 2024, Abhyudaya International Shalaka Honor-2026, and Kalidas Honor. Lucknow received 13 Padma Awards in 5 years In the past five years, the capital received 13 Padma Awards. Out of these, 10 awards were received during three years. In 2025, Dr. Sonia Nityanand - Medicine, Hriday Narayan Dixit - Literature and Education, and Satyapal Singh - Sports were honored with Padma Awards. In 2024, four luminaries, including SGPGI Director Dr. RK Dhiman, received this honor.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:All 3 Shankaracharyas back Avimukteshwaranand, says Sadanand Saraswati; Republic Day parade highlights Op Sindoor's integrated command centre more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. All 3 Shankaracharyas back Avimukteshwaranand, says Sadanand Saraswati Dwarka Sharda Peeth Shankaracharya Swami Sadanand Saraswati says all three Shankaracharyas support Avimukteshwaranand and questions the administration’s authority to seek any certificate. He condemns police action, calling the assault on innocent Brahmins reprehensible, while speaking at the Narmada Janmotsav in Jabalpur. 2. Republic Day parade highlights Op Sindoor's integrated command centre Republic Day parade showcased the Integrated Command used in Operation Sindoor, highlighting India’s modern defence coordination and strategic preparedness. A spectacular flypast featured 29 aircraft, including Sukhoi and Rafale jets, adding grandeur to the celebrations. 3. Bahraich road accident kills three youths as car crashes into tree A WagonR car hits a tree on a highway in Bahraich, killing three youths on the spot as the vehicle shatters completely. Two others, friends of the deceased, are critically injured and undergoing treatment in the hospital. 4. Chinese General Accused of Leaking Nuclear Secrets to United States China’s CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia is under investigation for allegedly sharing nuclear weapons information with the US. The allegation was reported by The Wall Street Journal, citing American intelligence sources. 5. Teacher slits student’s throat in Kanpur Dehat An 11th-grade student was allegedly murdered by his teacher in Kanpur Dehat after being called near the school and attacked with a knife. The 17-year-old named the teacher before dying during treatment. Police cite a money dispute; the accused is absconding. 6. Akhilesh’s soft outreach signals recalibration before 2027 Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s recent conciliatory moves, visiting the CM’s aide, backing Shankaracharya, and offering humanitarian help are being seen as a strategic attempt to broaden his appeal beyond PDA and soften political edges ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh polls. 7. Govt plans for facial recognition in Aadhaar instead of fingerprints The government has begun work on major changes to Aadhaar’s technical system under a new document called Aadhaar Vision 2032. Facial recognition is planned to replace fingerprints as the main identification method. 8. Western disturbances sharpen cold across U.P. Cold conditions intensified across Uttar Pradesh as two western disturbances set in. Rain is forecast on January 27–28, with night temperatures dropping 2–5°C and fog in the Terai. Azamgarh recorded the State’s lowest temperature at 6°C. 9. I won’t become a sadhvi for donations: Harsha Richariya Mahakumbh figure Harsha Richariya said she never wanted to monetise faith and faced sustained backlash from sections of the saint community. She announced plans to resume anchoring alongside religious outreach to remain financially independent, stressing that religion should reflect renunciation, not luxury. 10. Tilak Varma ruled out of last two T20Is against New Zealand India batter Tilak Varma will not play in the final two T20Is of the series against New Zealand as he recovers from an abdomen injury.

stories.title: Speeding car flips twice after tyre burst in Amroha:Two youths from Pilibhit die in accident, including HDFC bank manager and contractual computer operator
stories.summary: On Monday, a speeding out-of-control car jumped into the air when its tire burst in Amroha. Breaking the divider, it flipped twice. Then, sliding 15 feet away, it fell into the other lane. In the accident, two youths from Pilibhit traveling in the car died. One was a manager at HDFC Bank, while the other was a contractual computer operator. As soon as the accident happened, people present on the highway rushed to the car. Both youths were pulled out of the vehicle. One had died on the spot, while the other was critically injured and suffering. Police arrived after being informed of the incident and admitted the injured youth to the hospital, where he breathed his last. According to the police, the car's speed was over 100 kilometers per hour at the time of the accident. The accident occurred near Joya town in Didauli police station area, 5 kilometers away from the district headquarters. In the Haryana village of Didauli police station area, a speeding Beat car met with a terrible accident. Around 12 noon, Kshitij (35) and Shivank Saxena (40), who were traveling in the car, were returning to Pilibhit from Delhi. Suddenly, the car's tire burst. As the vehicle lost balance, it crashed into the divider. According to eyewitnesses, after hitting the divider, the car collided with a street light pole. Then, after flipping twice, it went into the second lane of the highway. The accident was so severe that the car was completely damaged. CCTV footage of the incident has also emerged, which shows the car bouncing in the air. Shivank Saxena from Kayasthan, Pilibhit, died on the spot in the accident. Meanwhile, Kshitij, who was driving the car, was seriously injured. Shivank was the branch manager at HDFC Bank in Pilibhit. Kshitij was working as a contractual computer operator at Puranpur block in Pilibhit. Both friends had gone to Delhi for some work The injured Kshitij was first taken to Joya Community Health Center, where, after primary treatment, seeing his serious condition, the doctors referred him to a higher center. Kshitij died during treatment here. Police investigation has revealed that the car belongs to Shivank. He was driving the car at the time of the accident. He and Kshitij had gone to Delhi for some work. The accident occurred while returning from there. Upon receiving information, Didauli police station reached the spot. The damaged car was removed. The body was sent for a post-mortem. Police are investigating the accident based on CCTV footage. Didauli Station Officer Harish Vardhan Singh said that two young men died in a road accident. The bodies have been kept in the mortuary. After identifying the bodies, the families of the deceased have been informed. Further action will be taken after their arrival.

stories.title: ‘Don’t act like my father,’ Khesari Yadav tells Ravi Kishan:Mimics BJP MP, mocks Pawan Singh, says, 'Gets tipsy after 2 pegs'
stories.summary: The verbal sparring between two superstars of Bhojpuri cinema continues to escalate. Actor Khesari Lal Yadav launched a direct attack on BJP MP from Gorakhpur and fellow actor Ravi Kishan, as well as on Pawan Singh, during a stage event. Khesari not only mimicked Ravi Kishan but also bluntly remarked that Ravi Kishan should not “try to act like my father”. He also took a swipe at Pawan Singh, saying that he “gets drunk after just two pegs”. Addressing an anchor on stage, Khesari said that jokes should be made only with those who can handle them, adding a remark about people with protruding bellies. His supporters claimed this comment was also a veiled taunt aimed at Pawan Singh. See pictures from Kolkata event What's the dispute between Ravi Kishan Khesari? Ravi Kishan and Pawan Singh were present on stage during the Gorakhpur Festival. During the programme, Ravi Kishan took a swipe at Khesari Lal Yadav while addressing the audience. Without naming him directly, Ravi Kishan remarked that there was an actor in the industry who, when he was new, used to show respect by touching both feet, but after gaining fame, had started touching only the knees. Pictures taken from Gorakhpur Festival Don't try to become my father: Khesari to Ravi Kishan In response to the remark, Khesari Lal Yadav recently mimicked Ravi Kishan during an event in Kolkata. Gesturing on stage, he said, “Earlier he used to touch here, now he touches here.” Khesari further remarked, “Be thankful that the person who shows you respect is like a brother. These days, even sons do not touch their father’s feet.” He added, “The man who gave birth to me is my father, Mangru Yadav, and no one should try to become my father.”

stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav Gears Up for UP 2027: समाजवादी पार्टी के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष एवं उत्तर प्रदेश के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अखिलेश यादव ने सन 2027 में होने वाले विधानसभा चुनावों को लेकर अपनी राजनीतिक सक्रियता तेज कर दी है। इसी क्रम में उन्होंने आज कैराना लोकसभा क्षेत्र की सांसद तथा पार्टी के अन्य प्रमुख नेताओं के साथ आगामी विधानसभा चुनावों की रणनीति पर विस्तार से चर्चा की। यह बैठक समाजवादी पार्टी के राज्य मुख्यालय, लखनऊ में आयोजित हुई, जहां क्षेत्रीय चुनावी समीकरणों, संगठन की स्थिति और मौजूदा राजनीतिक परिस्थितियों पर गहन विचार-विमर्श किया गया। बैठक में कैराना लोकसभा क्षेत्र की सांसद इकरा हसन, पूर्व सांसद तबस्सुम हसन सहित कई वरिष्ठ एवं स्थानीय नेता विशेष रूप से मौजूद रहे। चर्चा के दौरान अखिलेश यादव ने लोकसभा क्षेत्र के नेताओं से जमीनी हालात, मतदाता रुझान, सामाजिक समीकरण और संगठनात्मक मजबूती पर विस्तृत जानकारी ली।

stories.title: Bahraich road accident kills 3 youths after car crash:WagonR hits tree on highway, vehicle shatters completely; 2 friends critically injured and hospitalised
stories.summary: A terrible road accident occurred in Bahraich. A WagonR car crashed into a tree. This caused the car to shatter into pieces. Three friends, including the branch manager of a finance company, died on the spot in the accident. Two young men in the car were seriously injured. Police received information from passersby and took all the youths to the hospital. The accident happened around 4 am on Monday near Semarhana village on Nanpara-Lakhimpur Road in the Motipur police station area. 2 pictures of the accident... Abhishek Shukla (25), a resident of the Dhusah area of Balrampur, was a branch manager at Shriram Finance. He, along with his friends Deepu Verma (18), resident of Civil Line, Nitish Singh (19), resident of Alinagar, Ajay Sharma, and Lavkush Sharma, left for Kaichi Dham in Uttarakhand late Sunday evening in his WagonR car (UP 47 U 2214). Car hit tree at 4 AM Monday Around 4 AM on Monday, the car lost control and crashed into a tree on the highway near Semarhana village on the Nanpara-Lakhimpur route. The collision was so severe that the car was completely shattered. The front portion was badly damaged. The car's roof separated from the chassis. All occupants were badly trapped in the car seats. Passersby informed the police Passersby informed the police. Upon this, Motipur station in-charge Anand Chaurasia reached the spot with the police force. Police rescued all people trapped in the car and sent them to Motipur CHC by ambulance. During this, doctors declared Abhishek Shukla, Deepu Verma, and Nitish Singh dead. The injured Ajay Sharma and Lavkush Sharma were sent to the district hospital for treatment. Abhishek's father is retired from bank Abhishek's father, Sadanand Shukla, worked as a clerk in Sarv UP Gramin Bank. Deepu Verma's father, Dinesh, is involved in farming. The third deceased, Nitish's father Manoj, has passed away. Injured Ajay's father has also passed away. He used to manage the restaurant with his brother Balram, while Lovekush works in the timber business. Station in-charge Anand Chaurasia said - The accident happened around 4 am. Three youths died on the spot. The bodies of the deceased have been sent for post-mortem. The family has been informed.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets Satua Baba while hitting out at Yogi:Claims temples demolished, govt misleading people through publicity campaigns
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav hit back at CM Yogi, saying - Some people wake up from sleep but don't come to their senses. Their eyes remain closed all day, and even when awake, they remain intoxicated. He said, "I've heard there are some Satua Baba and Bathua Baba." But the weather is of Bathua. Therefore, we need to be very careful about people who deceive us through ads. They are deceiving us through publicity. Think about where the country has reached and where it should have gone. The country should run on the constitution, and decisions should be made according to the constitution. Former CM Akhilesh was addressing party workers on Republic Day on Monday. He said - Today even Shankaracharya is facing a crisis. Bulldozers are being run on temples that should have been protected. Read the key points of Akhilesh Yadav's address... 1- Crisis emerging for Shankaracharya, bulldozers running over temples Akhilesh Yadav said - Today, temples are being demolished. A crisis is emerging for Shankaracharya. Bulldozers are being run on temples that should have been protected. Aiming Satua Baba, he said that I have heard there is some Satua Baba, some Bathua Baba. It's the season of Bathua. 2- Government can bow down to America anytime They said that one day the Indian government will bow down. Non-veg milk products from America will also come to India. Think what will happen to our saints and sages if this happens? How will they keep their fasts? Our mothers and sisters who observe fasts. 3- Some people remain unconscious even after waking up from sleep SP chief said - Today something amazing happened... I was watching an saying that we are making India self-reliant. This is also being said by a foreign company. Who are they trying to deceive? Some people wake up from sleep but don't come to their senses. Those whose eyes remain closed all day remain intoxicated even after waking up. We need to be very careful of such people. 4- When they started losing, they brought SIR Akhilesh Yadav said - Those who are losing have brought SIR. They are not doing SIR but NRC. Aiming at the Prime Minister's Mann Ki Baat, he said that he was talking about votes. The government is making full efforts to get the votes cancelled. If votes get cancelled, then the question of citizenship will arise. Because every citizen has the right to vote. They are first taking away voting rights, then where will you go? We need to be careful of them. 5- Farmers' situation has gone from bad to worse On the farmers' issue, Akhilesh reminded that the government had promised to double farmers' income, but the situation has gone from bad to worse. Now with the arrival of foreign products and non-veg milk products, cultural and religious traditions could be affected, which will harm sadhus-saints and fasting mothers-sisters. Now know who Satua Baba is? Satua Baba lives at the Satua Baba Peeth in Varanasi. He is the 7th Peethadhishwar and Mahamandaleshwar of the Vishnu Swami sect. He came into discussion during the ongoing Magh Mela in Prayagraj when DM Manish Verma visited his camp ashram and cooked rotis for him. CM Yogi, who came to visit the fair, also visited his ashram. He is also known for his luxury vehicles.

stories.title: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri resigns:Upset over alleged assault on Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's disciples
stories.summary: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri resigned from his post on Republic Day in Uttar Pradesh. He cited the new UGC law and the alleged assault on disciples of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand as the reasons behind his decision. Agnihotri was seen standing outside his official residence holding a poster that read- 'UGC ROLL BACK – Withdraw the black law. India will not tolerate the insult of Shankaracharya and saints. #BOYCOTT BJP #BOYCOTT BRAHMAN MP MLA…' 5-page resignation letter submitted Alankar Agnihotri also wrote a five-page letter in which he mentioned an incident during the Prayagraj Magh Mela, where disciples of the Shankaracharya were allegedly grabbed by their hair. He wrote that such incidents deeply disturb even an ordinary Brahmin from within. He stated that it appeared the administration and the present government were working against Brahmins and saints, and that their dignity was being undermined. He added that no one was speaking up for the Brahmin community. ‘Is there preparation for genocide of Brahmins?’ asks Agnihotri In his letter, Agnihotri raised a sharp question, asking whether preparations were being made for the genocide of Brahmins. A member of the Brahmin community himself, Alankar Agnihotri became a PCS officer in 2019, securing the 15th rank. Earlier, he had come into the spotlight after placing a photograph of Lord Hanuman in his office. Following this, members of the Bhim Army staged a protest in the collectorate, during which heated arguments were reported with the officer. Senior officials attempt to persuade magistrate In an effort to persuade him, the Additional District Magistrate along with three other officers, reached the City Magistrate’s residence. All four officials stayed for nearly an hour before leaving. No details of the discussions held during the meeting have been disclosed. Political workers and Brahmin groups arrive in support Leaders from several Brahmin organisations, along with workers from the Samajwadi Party and Congress, reached Alankar Agnihotri’s residence to meet him. Brahmin leaders also staged a protest outside his residence, expressing solidarity with the resigned magistrate. Shankaracharya reacts to resignation Reacting to the resignation, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said that the respect accorded to Shankaracharyas runs very deep in the hearts of followers of Sanatan Dharma. He added that the consequences of hurting this sentiment could be gauged from this very incident, and the government should assess the outcome carefully.

stories.title: ‘Kacha Badam’ fame Anjali Arora’s boyfriend arrested:Fake MP pass recovered from car; claims to be MP’s representative during checking
stories.summary: Meerut police have arrested Akash Sansanwal, boyfriend of ‘Kacha Badam’ fame Anjali Arora, for using a fake pass of a former MP on his car. He was stopped during checking at the Kashi Toll Plaza, where the pass was found to be fake, leading to his arrest. Sources say Anjali Arora visited the police station 2–3 times to meet him. The arrest took place during heightened Republic Day security checks, with intensive verification underway at Meerut’s toll plazas for the past two days. During this drive, three other people, including Akash, were arrested on Sunday. Ex-MP's pass affixed Akash claims to be PA to former Delhi MP Akash Sansanwal is a resident of Katwaria Sarai, Kishan Garh Police Station, Delhi. He is the fianc of social media influencer, dancer, and model Anjali Arora. Anjali Arora has gained special recognition on social media with the song 'Kacha Badam' and is famous by the name 'Badam Girl'. Akash claims to be the PA of former Delhi MP Ramesh Bidhuri. He also states that former MP's son Sanjay Bidhuri is his close friend. Akash's fiance came to the police station to meet him on Sunday night and again this morning. She pleaded with the police to release her fiancé. Meanwhile, the police have now taken Akash for a medical examination. His medical examination is being conducted at the CHC. Additionally, while checking on the expressway, the police seized five vehicles that had fake MP and MLA passes. Action has also been taken against those car drivers. Action against 16 vehicle drivers Furthermore, action has been taken against 16 vehicles and their drivers for violating traffic rules, including applying black film on cars. CO Brahmapuri Saumya Asthana stated that the vehicles had fake MLA and MP passes. Cases were registered against Akash Sansanwal, Ashish, Kapil Prajapati, Danish Chaudhary, and Karamveer Singh, and their vehicles were seized.
