stories.title: Avimukteshwarananda demands Yogi prove his Hindu identity in 40 days:Says, 'Declare cow as Gaumata, or the saffron robe is just for show'
stories.summary: The dispute between the Prayagraj Magh Mela administration and Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand is continuing. Meanwhile, the Shankaracharya held a press conference in Varanasi. He said that in today’s time, demanding protection of cows and a ban on cow slaughter has become the biggest crime. He said that whenever anyone raised their voice against cow slaughter, governments tried to suppress it. He alleged that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and his associate Rambhadracharya are currently surrounding and attacking those who demand a ban on cow slaughter in different ways. The Shankaracharya said that he was even asked to show proof of being a Shankaracharya, whereas religion does not depend on any certificate. He alleged that attempts are being made to damage his image within the Sanatani community and that people connected to those in power are behind this. He said that when he was asked for a certificate, he provided it, but now the Chief Minister should give proof of being a Hindu. According to him, being a Hindu is not limited to speeches or clothing, but is linked to cow service and protection of religion. What has happened so far On January 18, while Avimukteshwaranand was going for a ritual bath at the Magh Mela, police stopped his palanquin. When his followers protested, there was pushing and shoving. Allegations were made that disciples were dragged by their hair. After this, the Shankaracharya sat on a protest outside his camp and did not enter it for 11 days. The administration issued two notices within two days, asking for proof of him being a Shankaracharya. Avimukteshwaranand replied to both notices. Chief Minister Yogi, without taking any name, referred to “Kalanemi”, which further deepened the dispute. In response, Avimukteshwaranand compared Yogi to Kalanemi and Aurangzeb. The saint community became divided into two groups over the issue, while all three Shankaracharyas supported Avimukteshwaranand. The Shankaracharya demanded that the administration apologise, only then would he take the holy bath. In his support, Bareilly City Magistrate resigned on January 26. After 24 hours, Ayodhya Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar resigned in support of the Chief Minister. On the morning of January 28, the Shankaracharya left the Magh Mela. This sudden development surprised everyone. He said that his heart was deeply hurt, and that he was leaving without taking the holy dip.

stories.title: Students dance in burqa at Gonda Republic Day program:College management apologizes costume selection, DIOS orders investigation
stories.summary: At a college Republic Day program in Gonda, female students were seen dancing on stage wearing burqas, triggering widespread outrage after a video of the incident surfaced. Reports claim that in the video, more than six Hindu students perform Bollywood songs while dressed in burqas. The video originates from Guru Charan Srivastava AR Inter College. Following protests by local residents at the college, the management issued a written apology on social media. The college clarified that a dance performance was intended on a horror-themed song, but the costumes were mistakenly selected. They also stated that the background music had been edited on social media, presenting the performance in a misleading manner. DIOS orders investigation, principal and manager summoned The District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) has ordered a formal investigation into the matter. The college principal and manager have been summoned for questioning. The incident took place in Nirmal Nagar Ballipur, under the Manakapur police station area, approximately 35 kilometers from the district headquarters. Dainik Bhaskar has not independently verified the viral videos. Community outrage and social media response The video has provoked anger among both Hindu and Muslim communities. Social media users have described the act as offensive to religious sentiments. Questions have been raised about the school administration’s oversight, and many have demanded strict action against the responsible individuals. Critics have warned that if such incidents occur in schools, it undermines the institution’s credibility. Multiple organizations have expressed objections to the video online. College management issues apology Seeing the controversy escalate, college manager Raju Srivastava issued a written apology. While submitting the apology at Manakapur police station, he stated that during the Republic Day program, students performed a “ghost team” mixed song as part of the cultural event. He expressed regret if anyone’s sentiments were hurt and apologized on behalf of the school family. The manager also confirmed that no such program would be organized in the future. DIOS orders full investigation Taking the viral video seriously, DIOS Dr. Ramchandra has directed a comprehensive investigation. Further actions will be based on the findings. Both the college principal and manager have been summoned for questioning. Investigation ordered, college manager and principal summoned DIOS Dr. Ramchandra said- The viral video has come to our attention, in which some female students are seen dancing while wearing burqas. This video is said to be from Republic Day. The college management and principal have been summoned. I am personally investigating the entire matter. Action will be taken based on whatever facts come to light in the investigation.

stories.title: Greater Noida female influencer faces 27 km chase by youths:Calls husband as men continue making obscene gestures while she drives home
stories.summary: A case has emerged in Greater Noida involving a well-known female social media influencer being chased by car-riding youths. It is alleged that from Delhi’s DND Flyover to Pari Chowk in Greater Noida, the youths followed her for nearly 27 kilometers. They repeatedly tried to overtake her. Hanging out of the moving car windows, the youths made obscene gestures. The chase continued until the woman reached her home. Frightened, she stopped her car and called her husband to inform him about the incident. During this time, the accused were also standing near the scene. Since she was close to home, her husband arrived at the spot quickly. He contacted the police and provided complete details of the incident. Until the police reached the location, arguments continued between the accused and the woman’s husband. Meanwhile, officers from the Knowledge Park police station arrived and spoke to both parties. However, the woman refused to file a formal complaint, so the police advised the accused and released them. The husband later shared a video of the incident on social media. The woman has 5.7 million followers on Instagram, while her husband has over 2 million followers. The woman was returning home in a BMW, and the youths blocked her car from the front at multiple points. Police had intended to arrest and send the accused to jail, but the woman and her husband, identified as Lakhan and Neetu, refused. Incident in Sequence January 27: Returning Home in a BMW The woman’s husband said that on January 27, his wife was returning from Delhi to their home in Greater Noida in a BMW. Near the DND Flyover, some youths riding in another car began following her vehicle. On the way, they repeatedly tried to overtake her and made obscene gestures. The Woman Called Her Husband in Fear The husband added that when the youths continued following her near Pari Chowk, she became extremely frightened. Panicked, she called him and explained the entire incident. At that time, their home was approximately 15 minutes away. Upon receiving the information, he immediately rushed to the location and informed the police. The Knowledge Park police station subsequently arrived at the scene. Police Warn Accused and Release Them According to the husband, the police spoke to both parties. Arrangements were being made to send the accused to jail, but the woman refused to lodge a complaint. Following this, the police issued warnings to the accused and released them.

stories.title: Prayagraj administration to apologize to Avimukteshwaranand:Shankaracharya sets 2 conditions, while 2 senior Lucknow officials to ensure respected Sangam Snan ceremony
stories.summary: The Prayagraj administration has reportedly agreed to apologize to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, according to the spiritual leader’s media representative Yogiraj Sarkar. The announcement comes after Shankaracharya abruptly left the Magh Mela for Varanasi, shocking officials who had expected him to stay until the Mela’s full moon bathing ceremony on February 1. Two senior officials from Lucknow contacted Shankaracharya after his arrival in Varanasi, promising him a respected Sangam bath on the Mela’s Purnima day. The Shankaracharya set two conditions for the administration: Officials from the state will accompany Shankaracharya back to Prayagraj for the ceremonial bath. High-level meeting on January 27: Points of disagreement The conflict between Shankaracharya and the administration lasted 11 days, beginning with the Mauni Amavasya bathing incident. On January 27 evening, a secret high-level meeting was held at the Dharm Sangh camp near Shankaracharya’s tent. Present at the meeting were Rishi Raj and Deputy Mela Officer Dayanand Prasad, along with other Mela officials. Representing Shankaracharya was Mahant Shridharanand Brahmachari from Mankameshwar Temple. Shankaracharya’s disciples did not attend the meeting. Three points were agreed upon by both sides: However, two key issues remained unresolved: Mahant Shridharanand insisted that without a written apology, Shankaracharya would not accept their apology. In 2 pictures, see the scenes of Shankaracharya leaving the Magh Mela and the ashram being removed- Incident timeline and Background Shankaracharya explains decision to leave Mela Before leaving, Shankaracharya addressed the media, saying: I am deeply saddened to leave without taking the bath. I came here with faith and devotion, but an incident occurred that I never expected. Those who insulted Sanatan traditions must be held accountable. He rejected a proposal from the administration to hold the Sangam bath, stating that anger and hurt prevent peace, even in holy waters. Yogiraj Sarkar added that Shankaracharya’s decision was also influenced by the assault on his disciples during Mauni Amavasya.

stories.title: SP MP is protecting Moid Khan:Ayodhya rape victim’s mother alleges DNA report was manipulated, fears for her safety, and will approach the High Court
stories.summary: "Samajwadi Party MP Moid Khan is being protected, I think even the test report has been altered. How can we forget what happened to my daughter?" mother of the rape victim A daughter was raped on July 29, 2024. Samajwadi Party leader Moid Khan and his servant Raju Khan were accused in the case. POCSO Court Judge Nirupama Vikram has acquitted Moid Khan. His servant Raju Khan was found guilty and sentenced to 20 years in prison. Moid Khan will remain in jail for now because a separate case under the Gangster Act is also registered against him. The victim’s family is still in deep pain, say reports. Read the report The Bhaskar team reached the home of the rape victim living in the Bhadarsa area of Ayodhya. There was silence at the gate, and CCTVs were installed on the front pillar. Their light was drawing attention. Inside the house, the rape victim, her mother, and brother were found. The mother spoke to us with a heavy heart. Read the full conversation Question: Was the advocacy on your behalf not done properly? Answer: Everyone knows Moid Khan did wrong. I don't know how the court is letting him go. We are not educated, so advocacy could not be done on our behalf. The police did not investigate properly, otherwise, Moid would not have been released. This is not right, our hearing was not done properly. Question: Raju Khan was sentenced to 20 years in prison and a fine of 50 thousand? Answer: He (Raju) should not get 20 years in prison, he should be hanged. He has ruined my daughter's life, his house should also be demolished. Now we will go to the High Court. Question: Will you be in danger if Moid Khan is released? Answer: Even when these people were in jail, we were scared. Now that we've heard Moid Khan is being released, the danger has increased. Ever since my daughter was raped, we have stayed inside the house, but for how long will we stay. Now it will be difficult to go out. We demand security, the police used to come before, but now no one comes. There are 2 CCTV cameras installed outside our house, which were installed by the police, and we monitor with them. Question: Has Moid Khan received a clean chit in the DNA report? Answer: We are not satisfied with the DNA test. Something went wrong. These MPs are protecting Moeed Khan, which is why our hearing is not happening. The test report has been altered, how can we forget what happened to my daughter. Raju's DNA also matched On July 29, 2024, a 12-year-old girl filed a gangrape case in the Bhadarsa area of Ayodhya. The girl was pregnant at that time. Moeed Khan and his servant Raju Khan were named as accused in this. Moeed and Raju were arrested the next day after the FIR was registered. Later, on August 7, 2024, the minor rape survivor's abortion was performed at Queen Mary's Hospital in Lucknow, following a court order. The victim alleged that she worked with Raju Khan, and about two and a half months ago, Raju had introduced her to Moeed. In the complaint filed at the police station, she claimed that Moeed, along with his servant, raped her. They recorded a video of this incident. Using the video to intimidate and threaten her, Moeed and Raju continued to sexually exploit her for about two and a half months. Now, Moeed has been proven innocent in court, while his servant Raju has been found involved in the incident by the court. Raju's DNA also matched the DNA of the fetus. UP government had run a bulldozer After this incident, the administration had demolished Moid's bakery and shopping mall. At that time, the then District Magistrate of Ayodhya, Chandra Vijay Singh, had said - Moid Khan's bakery was illegally built on pond land, which is why action was taken. CM Yogi, while giving a statement in the assembly, claimed Moied Khan's association with the SP. He had said - Moied in Ayodhya, who is a leader of the Samajwadi Party and a member of the MP's team in Ayodhya, has been found involved in the rape of a 12-year-old minor girl. The Chief Minister had also met the family of the rape victim after the case was registered. Following this, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had demanded DNA tests for Moied and Raju. Moeed got an advantage on 4 points in court Advocate Saeed Khan, who defended Moeed, told a media channel that the results of the DNA test were most crucial in this decision. The court considered Moeed innocent and 'honorably acquitted' him. 1. A DNA test of the fetus was conducted on the court's order, which did not match Moeed's DNA. 2. The prosecution could not even prove where the incident took place. The prosecution presented a total of 13 witnesses in support of the rape victim. 3. It was also claimed that a video was made during the incident, but no video was presented as evidence in court. 4. Contradictions have also emerged regarding the crime scene during the police investigation. During the police investigation, different claims were made about the incident occurring both under a tree outside the bakery and inside the bakery. Speaking to the media, Special Public Prosecutor Virendra Kumar said- This decision will be challenged in the High Court. We will continue to fight the case.

stories.title: Kanpur road built in just 24 hours:Susbstandard materials used, surface breaks under bicycles and pedestrians walking on the road
stories.summary: A scam has come to light in Jhandapur village, Ghatampur tehsil, Kanpur, over a 400-meter road that broke within a day. The road was built in just 24 hours, but villagers said it became unusable the next day. Gravel came loose even when the bicycle brakes were applied, and potholes appeared when villagers stepped on it. Villagers protested, but the contractor finished the work, packed the machines, and left. Now, they have filed a complaint on the Chief Minister’s portal and plan to approach the District Magistrate’s office. When a Bhaskar reporter visited the site, villagers showed the poor condition of the road. See 2 pictures- Contractors built the road and left in 24 hours Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Jhandapur village, about 55 kilometers from Kanpur. Abhay, Saurabh, Govind, Sumit, Sunil, Puneet, Manish, and Ravindra from the village showed us the reality of the road on the spot. According to the villagers, contractor Piyush Kushwaha started the work late at night and built the road within 24 hours. However, the construction, done by disregarding standards, is now crumbling in many places, and the road has caved in in several sections. Villagers said - Roller not used, material substandard Villagers allege that during road construction, neither proper filling was done nor was a road roller used. As a result, the road has sunk from the edges. The villagers say that substandard material was used; the situation is such that if a cyclist applies brakes, the road starts to crumble. Work done at night despite protests Villagers said that they had protested against the substandard construction, but the contractor did not listen to anyone. The work was completed overnight and the machines were removed. After the condition of the road came to light, officials were called to complain and the matter was also registered on the CM portal. District Panchayat member had raised questions earlier Rajnarayan Kuril, District Panchayat member from Patari, had recently written a letter to Kanpur DM Jitendra Pratap Singh, alleging a scam in a four hundred meter road. He had accused contractor Piyush Kushwaha of disregarding standards and manipulating measurements in the construction work. The DM had assured investigation and action. Claim of irregularities in works worth crores The District Panchayat member alleges that the concerned contractor's firm has carried out works worth 4 to 5 crore rupees for CC roads, asphalt roads, and paved roads in the District Panchayat area. Similar irregularities are suspected in all these works as well. He has demanded a high-level investigation into all the works. District Panchayat President remained silent On the question of the road scam and irregularities, District Panchayat President Swapnil Varun remained silent. When contacted, the call was disconnected, stating that he was in a meeting. Villagers demand - investigation, action against those responsible The villagers of Jhandapur say that if action is not taken in time, they will reach the DM office and protest. They clearly state - the road is paved on paper, but not on the ground. The scam should be investigated, and all those responsible should be acted upon.

stories.title: Dense fog returns in UP, rain alert for 3 days:Visibility drops to 10 meters, icy winds sweep through cities, leaving people shivering amid severe cold conditions
stories.summary: Dense fog envelops Uttar Pradesh today. Around 30 districts, including Lucknow, Jhansi, Agra and Aligarh, have remained under dense fog since Friday morning. In several districts such as Aligarh and Jhansi, visibility has dropped to as low as 10 metres. Strong icy winds have intensified the cold during morning and evening hours, while dew drops are being felt like light drizzling rain. Roads appeared largely deserted. People stepping out of vehicles complained of numbness in their hands. Those venturing out for essential work were seen wrapped in warm clothing. Bonfires were lit at several places along roadsides to combat the cold. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for the next three to four days, raising the possibility of another spell of severe cold. According to the Meteorological Department, a fresh western disturbance is becoming active over the state from February 1. Due to its impact, rainfall is likely in both western and eastern parts of Uttar Pradesh between February 1 and February 3. Senior scientist at Meteorological Center Lucknow, Atul Kumar Singh said - Minimum temperatures across the state may drop by 3 to 5 degrees in the next 24 hours. Light fog may persist in eastern and terai regions. Condition of major cities Lucknow: Light haze and fog prevailed in the morning. Icy winds made the cold more severe. The maximum temperature is expected to be around 21 degrees Celsius, while the minimum may hover near 10 degrees. On Thursday, the minimum temperature was recorded at 11.2 degrees Celsius. Jhansi: Dense fog prevailed in the morning, with visibility around 10 metres. The minimum temperature was recorded at 10 degrees Celsius. The Utkal Express travelling from Haridwar to Puri was delayed by 12 hours, while 15 other trains are also running behind schedule. Agra: Dense fog prevailed in the morning, accompanied by icy winds that increased the chill. Fog remained lighter within the city but denser in outer areas. The morning temperature was around 8 degrees Celsius. Dew drops felt like rain. The AQI was recorded at 266, falling in the moderate category. Aligarh: Dense fog prevailed in the morning with visibility around 10 metres. Cold winds intensified the chill. The maximum temperature was recorded at 19 degrees Celsius and the minimum at 8 degrees Celsius. How will the weather be for 3 days January 31: Fog likely in some districts, with winds blowing at speeds of 30–40 km per hour. February 1: Rain likely in many parts of eastern and western UP. February 2: Rain likely in many parts of eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, along with strong winds. January rainfall 39% below normal January remained dull in terms of rainfall this year. According to Meteorological Department data, Lucknow received 8.6 mm of rainfall in January, against a normal average of 14.1 mm. This marks a deficiency of nearly 39 percent. Impact of fog in UP; Know how fog forms Crops suffer heavy damage due to rain, wind and hail Agriculture expert Siddharth Singh said that if wheat crops lodge due to strong winds, grain weight reduces, potentially leading to a production loss of up to 20 percent. Sugarcane crops have also lodged extensively, raising concerns over cane damage and reduced yield. Mustard and vegetable crops have suffered significant damage due to rain. Excess waterlogging in fields has caused mustard pods to fall to the ground, increasing the risk of grain damage. Waterlogging has also led to rotting in vegetable crops. Farmers engaged in vegetable cultivation have suffered the maximum losses due to the recent weather conditions.

stories.title: Girls escape 'captivity' to meet boyfriends:Made rope from dupatta in Mathura, scaled 35-feet wall hiding from CCTV; all traced and brought back in shelter home
stories.summary: Five girls made a daring escape from a women’s shelter home in Mathura, smartly picking January 26, when most staff members were exhausted after Republic Day duties. Around 10 PM, the girls climbed to the shelter’s rooftop and used dupattas and blankets to twist a makeshift rope, which they used to scale down the nearly 35-feet-high wall. Police traced and caught four of the girls within 24 hours from Delhi, Agra, Aligarh, and Mahavan, and brought them back to the shelter home. Meanwhile, the fifth girl, a resident of Nohzheel, was recovered from her home on January 28. During questioning, it was revealed that two girls from Delhi and Agra had fled to meet their boyfriends, against whom rape cases had already been registered. The other three girls were reportedly distressed by family issues and supported the plan, helping them execute the escape When the Agra girl called her boyfriend, he panicked and sent his girlfriend's location to the police through a lawyer. To find out how these girls escaped and made it back to the shelter home, Dainik Bhaskar visited the women's shelter home in Chaitanya Vihar. Read the ground report... Story of 2 girls who ran away to meet their boyfriends FIR of rape filed against boyfriend, expressed threat to life when found Chaitanya Vihar is among the posh areas of Vrindavan. The women's shelter home is built near the flyover here. All its arrangements are managed by the Women and Child Welfare Department. 8 months ago, the girls' protection home was also shifted to this campus. It houses POCSO Act victims and girls who are found after going missing from home. After discussions with officials, it came to light that currently 93 girls from Mathura, Vrindavan and nearby districts were staying in the shelter home. All the girls are between 14 to 17 years of age. In this shelter home, 2 girls from Agra and Delhi were also present. Their families had filed cases of kidnapping and rape against their boyfriends. The allegation was that the boys misled our daughters and kidnapped them. Then raped them. Actually, these girls were in love affairs. The girls had run away from home with their boyfriends. In the family, fathers and brothers had filed rape FIRs against the boyfriends to trap them. When the police recovered the girls, they refused to go with their families. Since they were minors, they had expressed fear for their lives. Therefore, they were kept in the shelter home. Stole key under pretense of helping staff Both girls from Agra and Delhi were brought to Mathura's shelter home. The love stories of both girls were similar. Both started living in the same common room. Meanwhile, they quickly became friends. Both shared their stories with each other. On January 20, the girls planned that they needed to escape from this confinement. They were worried about how their boyfriends and family members would be doing. They wanted to meet them. The girls first understood the structure of the entire shelter home building. They found no weak points. The walls were quite high. CCTV cameras were installed everywhere. The girls realized that after reaching the roof, there was no way out except jumping from a height of 35 feet. However, the gate leading to the stairs to the roof was kept locked. The girls understood that if they wanted to escape, they would need the key to this lock. They first stole the key to the stairway gate under the pretense of helping the shelter home staff with their work. After this, they waited for 1 day. Girls' plan leaked to 3 more girls The escape plan of the girls became known to 3 more girls living with them. Those three were brought to the shelter home in different POCSO Act cases. This way, by January 25, the number of girls planning to escape reached 5. All the girls planned together that January 26th would be the best day to escape. Because, officers and staff would remain busy throughout the day in Republic Day programs. At 10 PM when everyone had dinner and went to sleep, the girls came out of their respective rooms. After unlocking the stairs, they reached the hostel roof. All of them had brought dupattas and blankets with them. They sat on the roof and tied these together to make a rope-like structure. Then they tied it to the water tank pipe and started descending slowly. However, since the rope was too short, all five had to jump from a height of 15 feet. During this, the girl from Delhi injured her foot. The story after escaping from the shelter Called boyfriend from lounge, 1 boyfriend got scared The girls from Agra and Delhi told police that they managed to reach a lounge while trying to protect themselves. Here they made an excuse of injury. Then they called their boyfriends using someone's mobile phone. They informed them that they had escaped from the shelter home to meet them. 3 girls ran away home, caught from there The other 3 girls, who had fled from the shelter home on the pretext of helping, were also found at their respective homes. One girl's mother is not alive, and her father is in jail. When the father came out of jail on parole, he accused his sister's brother-in-law of eloping with the girl. After the girl was found, she was sent to the shelter home. The second girl had an affair with her aunt's son. In this case, the girl's mother and brother were opposing. However, her brother had also done a love marriage. In this case, when the girl was recovered, the mother said at the police station that they have nothing to do with her anymore, so she was sent to the shelter home. Girls seen in lobby CCTV, then disappeared On the morning of January 27, the shelter home staff discovered that 5 girls were missing. The home's superintendent Gayatri Mishra informed the administration officials and police. SSP Shlok Kumar arrived at the home. Police checked CCTV footage, the girls were visible in lobby cameras. However, there were no CCTV cameras installed at the spot from where they escaped. This caused initial difficulty in searching. Police kept searching for the girls in small hotels and lounges around the shelter home. A lounge revealed that 2 girls had come there that night. One had an injury on her foot. She had said that a car hit me. After this, she left from there at 8 am on Tuesday.

stories.title: Transgender skin therapist performs spiritual penance at Magh Mela:Says, 'Govt schemes for community are still not fully implemented'
stories.summary: Priyanshi Das, a transgender skin therapist from Prayagraj, shared her life story at the ongoing Magh Mela. “I was 7-8 years old when I realised my body didn’t match how I felt inside. I was born male, but my mind and identity were female. I loved dressing up and preparing myself like a girl,” she said. Priyanshi faced taunts from society and struggled to fit in during school and college. Despite attempts to discuss her feelings with her family, she found no support. “No one at home understood me, so I left and joined the transgender community,” she added. A large number of people come to her and take selfies. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke to her in detail. Besides her, they also spoke to some other Kinnars. They understood the facilities and conveniences provided by the government. Let's find out what they shared… Joining the transgender community and pursuing education Priyanshi’s new community embraced her, and she completed her education. Today, she works as a cosmetologist and skin therapist, practicing in Odisha and Mumbai. She also became an activist, raising awareness about HIV/AIDS within the transgender community. “The transgender community faces discrimination in education and society. That’s why we started an organization to promote education and awareness. Initially, there were very few educated people in our society, and support was minimal. But persistence brought change,” she said. Spiritual practice at Magh Mela At the Magh Mela in Sector 6, where the transgender Akhara has a prominent presence, Priyanshi is currently performing spiritual practices and blessing devotees. Large crowds gather for blessings and selfies. She gives a coin and rice as a token of blessings. Supreme Court recognition and Government gaps The landmark 2014 Supreme Court ruling recognized transgender people as a third gender and directed the government to provide education and health services. “The decision gave us legal recognition, but many government schemes are not fully implemented. Reservation and job opportunities are still limited,” Priyanshi said. Mahamandaleshwar Kaushalya Giri of the Sanatan Transgender Akhara explained, “In Bihar, transgender people were given opportunities in police recruitment and home guard. But Uttar Pradesh has yet to implement similar provisions. We want even 1% reservation guaranteed; that’s enough to ensure stability for our community.” Challenges on the ground Mahamandaleshwar Sanjana Nand Giri, also from the Sanatan Akhara, emphasized the need for employment opportunities. “The younger generation needs education and jobs to avoid discrimination on the streets. Some states like Telangana, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand are implementing rules, including housing schemes. But much remains to be done,” she said.

stories.title: BJP's regional balance breaks down in UP:Gorakhpur and Kashi dominate Purvanchal, Awadh and western regions weaken
stories.summary: The regional balance in the UP BJP government and organisation has been disrupted. The dominance of the Kashi and Gorakhpur regions of Purvanchal has increased in key positions in both the government and the organisation, while Awadh and the western region remain the weakest. Political observers say that with the upcoming Assembly elections, the BJP will have to correct this imbalance, as its continuation could impact electoral outcomes. The BJP traditionally focuses on maintaining regional and social balance and often makes efforts to strike such equilibrium. However, this time both Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary hail from Gorakhpur district. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya is also from the Kashi region of Purvanchal. A large number of office-bearers in the party organisation are from Purvanchal as well. In contrast, Awadh and the western region have not been given comparable preference even within the organisation. CM Yogi is from Purvanchal. The Deputy CM is also from the Kashi region of Purvanchal, while Brajesh Pathak belongs to the Awadh region. Three office-bearers from a single district In the BJP’s state team, there are instances of three office-bearers coming from the same district. Several office-bearers have strategically changed their home district to Lucknow. State vice-presidents Trimbak Tripathi and Santosh Singh, along with general secretary Subhash Yaduvansh, are from Sant Kabir Nagar district. Similarly, vice-presidents Salil Vishnoi, Manvendra Singh, Kamalavati Singh and Devesh Kori are all from Kanpur district. Awadh and West lag behind in organisation too The BJP’s 45-member state team includes one state president, one general secretary (organisation), seven general secretaries, 18 vice-presidents and 16 ministers. Of these, five state vice-presidents, four of the seven general secretaries and five ministers are from Purvanchal. The western region does not have even a single state general secretary, though it has five vice-presidents and three state ministers. The Braj region has three state ministers, one general secretary and one vice-president. Awadh has four ministers and one general secretary, but not a single vice-president. Kanpur has one minister and four state vice-presidents, but no general secretary. New leadership fails to emerge Political analyst Virendra Nath Bhatt says that Purvanchal’s influence within the BJP is currently much higher, even though Awadh delivered the highest number of seats. He notes that when regional balance is not maintained, regions that lag behind in the organisation or government fail to produce new leadership. Shadow of UGC issue to remain Political analysts believe that although the Supreme Court has stayed the new UGC rules, the issue has not cooled down. Its impact will be visible in the formation of the BJP’s new team and the expansion of the cabinet in the coming period. Brahmins and Thakurs are likely to be given slightly more importance than before in the BJP team. In UP, the issue of Brahmin resentment is particularly prominent, and the BJP may give more opportunities to Brahmin faces to address it. Before 2014, Brahmins, Thakurs and Vaishyas had greater representation in the state team, but representation of the upper castes has steadily declined since then. Senior journalist Anand Rai says that the BJP suffered a major setback in Purvanchal, losing several seats there in the Lok Sabha elections. This is why more effort is now being focused on the region and its leaders are being promoted. He adds that despite being a large party, cabinet and state team positions are limited, making it impossible to provide leadership roles to all districts. Preparations to restore regional balance A BJP office-bearer said that organisational changes are expected in the coming days. A new team under state president Pankaj Chaudhary will be formed, and regional presidents of all six regions will also be changed. The party has realised that the regional balance has been disturbed. BJP leaders also acknowledge that this was one of the reasons behind the party’s defeat in 2024. As a result, in the upcoming organisational changes, the state and national leadership will attempt to restore regional balance to address the dissatisfaction among office-bearers.

In 2023, 54% of female suicides were married women, with housewives comprising 44%. This highlights significant marital and economic pressures impacting women's mental well-being in the capital.

stories.title: ‘It’s a nightmare’: UK man sues NHS after receiving eight years of chemotherapy instead of six months
stories.summary: A Warwickshire man is suing an NHS trust after alleged surgical and oncology failings left him with permanent brain and sight damage. David Bown was kept on chemotherapy for more than eight years, far beyond clinical guidance, after delayed post-operative scans and treatment errors. Lawyers say his case highlights systemic failures affecting dozens of patients.

stories.title: Pawar play in Maharashtra post dada's death: NCP factions eyeing February merger
stories.summary: Ajit Pawar's untimely death in a plane crash has reignited talks of reuniting the NCP factions. Sources indicate merger talks were advanced, with Ajit Pawar viewing it as a strategic move for the party's future. His passing may now accelerate this process, with a potential February announcement. Leadership questions arise for the ruling NCP.

stories.title: Real estate tycoon CJ Roy found dead in office; police suspect suicide

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Ramadan 2026 moon sighting date: KSA Supreme Court calls on Muslims to sight Al Hijri 1447 crescent

stories.title: Magh Mela row: Seer ups the ante; asks CM Yogi to prove he is 'Hindu sympathiser'
stories.summary: Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has asked UP CM Yogi Adityanath to stop beef exports from the state and declare the cow as ‘Rajya Mata’. The new rules notified by the UGC on January 13 -- the Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026 -- have sparked widespread criticism from general category students who argue that the framework could lead to discrimination against them.

stories.title: Vande Mataram front and centre at Republic Day
stories.summary: Republic Day celebrations prominently featured the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram,' with performances and tableaux across states. The national song's significance was highlighted, becoming a focal point for political discourse, particularly between the BJP and TMC ahead of West Bengal's assembly polls. Gujarat and Chhattisgarh, among others, showcased tributes to the patriotic anthem.

stories.title: Is an archaeological marvel hiding near Chandigarh?
stories.summary: Sirhind, once a significant historical hub, now lies neglected with its ancient monuments crumbling and forgotten. Despite its rich past, from the era of Prithviraj Chauhan to Guru Gobind Singh's sons, the town has faded from public consciousness. Archaeological exploration and preservation efforts are minimal, leaving its historical treasures buried and overlooked.

stories.title: Once again, Congress spars with BJP over its netas' seating
stories.summary: Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi's seating at the Republic Day parade sparked a row, with the BJP accusing the Congress of entitlement. The Congress countered, calling it "petty politicking" and an insult to the Constitution. This controversy echoes past seating disputes and a recent incident at the Red Fort.

stories.title: Stonehenge mystery solved? Study reveals how 25-tonne stones reached the site in southern England
Why Marco Rubio pretends to be a ‘mummy’ on Air Force One? Inside Trump’s sleepless flights
stories.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio described keeping up with President Trump on overseas trips as an endurance sport, admitting he disguises himself as a mummy to sleep on Air Force One. Trump reportedly "practically never" sleeps, often waking staff for conversations, making long flights a challenge for his team.

stories.title: From leading contingents to bike daredevilry, women steal the show atRepublic Day parade
stories.summary: Women military personnel shone at the 77th Republic Day parade, leading contingents, showcasing skills, and participating in key ceremonial events. From Flight Lieutenant Akshita Dhankar unfurling the flag to Captain Harshita Yadav leading an animal contingent and Captain Samira Z Buttar commanding a tableau, women made significant contributions.

stories.title: Op Sindoor: IAF releases video of Rafale armed with beyond-visual-range Meteor missile, silences sceptics
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force released a video showcasing its fighter jets armed with advanced missiles like Meteor and BrahMos, silencing critics who doubted India's possession of the beyond-visual-range Meteor missile. The footage featured Rafale, Sukhoi, and Tejas jets, confirming the missile's presence and capabilities for air-to-air combat.

stories.title: At R-Day parade, India showcases 'Sindoor' valour, as DRDO missile, Bhairav battalion make debut
stories.summary: India's military might, including lethal weapon systems and fighter jets from Operation Sindoor, captivated crowds on Kartavya Path during the 77th Republic Day parade. The event showcased advanced missile systems, air defence capabilities, and a unique 'Battle Array Format' with an aerial component, highlighting India's defence prowess to European dignitaries.

stories.title: Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino removed amid backlash over Pretti shooting; Kristi Noem also said to be at risk: Report
stories.summary: US Border Patrol's "commander at large," Gregory Bovino, has been removed following the fatal shooting of a US citizen by agents under his command. This demotion signals a potential shift in the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement tactics. President Trump and Minnesota Governor Walz have also adopted a more conciliatory tone after a call regarding the deportation drive.

stories.title: Agri scientists, farmers among Padma winners
stories.summary: Nine individuals from the farm and allied sectors, including prominent agricultural scientists Ashok Kumar Singh and Gopal Ji Trivedi, have been honored with the Padma Shri. Their contributions range from developing numerous rice varieties and genome-edited crops to promoting makhana cultivation and innovative farming techniques, significantly boosting farm growth and farmer livelihoods across India.

stories.title: FBI director Kash Patel’s firearm comment on Pretti shooting sparks Second Amendment debate — what is it?
Ursula von der Leyen: Successful India benefits world
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that a successful India contributes to global stability and prosperity. The presence of EU leaders at India's Republic Day parade highlighted the strengthening India-EU partnership and commitment to shared values, with a new security and defense pact expected to be signed.

stories.title: Kedarnath, Badrinath and 47 affiliated temples considering a ban on entry of non-Hindus
stories.summary: Following a proposal to restrict non-Hindus at Haridwar's Kumbh ghats, the Badrinath Kedarnath Temple Committee is considering a similar move at its shrines. Citing tradition and constitutional rights, the committee chairman stated the decision aims to preserve religious practices, welcoming those who respect their faith.

stories.title: On Padma rolls is man who 'exposed' UPA on Ishrat case
stories.summary: A former MHA officer, RVS Mani, instrumental in exposing contradictory affidavits in the Ishrat Jahan case, has been honored with the Padma Shri. Mani claimed political interference led to the revision of the initial affidavit, which cited intelligence reports confirming Jahan's terror links. The second affidavit downplayed the intelligence, a move later confirmed by then Home Minister Rajnath Singh.

stories.title: Coldest Republic Day in 5 years, rain likely today
stories.summary: Delhi experienced its coldest Republic Day since 2021, with temperatures dipping to 4.2°C at Safdarjung and 3.6°C in parts of the city, triggering cold wave conditions. Clear skies and northwesterly winds contributed to the chill. Light to moderate rain and thunderstorms are expected today, with a yellow alert issued.

stories.title: Brandon Paul breaks down after TikTok star MacKenzie Paul dies at 26 following three year battle with acute myeloid leukaemia
stories.summary: TikTok star MacKenzie Paul has died at 26 after a three-year fight with acute myeloid leukemia. Her husband, Brandon Paul, confirmed her death in an emotional Facebook video. According to People Magazine, MacKenzie became known for sharing her cancer journey openly, inspiring thousands before her passing

stories.title: Purdue campus talks gather pace; UK, Canadian univs signal interest
stories.summary: India's higher education is opening up to global players, with Purdue University's campus plans in advanced talks. Following policy shifts, British and Canadian institutions are also showing keen interest. This move, building on existing foreign university presences, aims to bring top-tier engineering and technology programs to India, allowing students to earn international degrees locally.

stories.title: Aggressive low bids put NHAI in a fix, trend may impact quality
stories.summary: Highway construction agencies are facing a challenge as contractors aggressively bid up to 48% below estimated project costs, raising concerns about work quality. This trend, driven by fewer projects and increased competition, forces contractors to quote low to keep resources engaged, potentially impacting the sector's long-term health and project standards.

stories.title: Congress says Modi government not serious about caste count in Census 2027
stories.summary: Congress has questioned the Modi government's intent regarding the caste enumeration in Census 2027, citing that the 'houselisting' questionnaire omits 'OBC' as an option. The party demands immediate consultations with political parties, states, and civil society before finalizing the caste census details.

stories.title: ‘Big armada’ near Iran: Trump says Tehran 'wants to talk, strike deal' amid rising tensions
stories.summary: President Trump announced a "big armada" is deployed near Iran, stating the situation remains in flux. While close to ordering strikes earlier this month, he delayed the decision, believing Tehran genuinely seeks a deal. The US has bolstered its military presence in the region, including an aircraft carrier strike group, as diplomatic options are also being considered.

stories.title: Congress brass may meet Shashi Tharoor to settle issues
stories.summary: Congress leadership is planning to meet senior leader Shashi Tharoor following his absence from a crucial Kerala election strategy meeting. Tharoor, who cited personal issues and unhappiness with the party, will be invited for discussions to address his grievances. The party aims to ensure unity for the upcoming state elections, recognizing Tharoor's electoral influence.

stories.title: Jessica Daugirdas dies at 35 after sharing her three-year colorectal cancer fight with followers
stories.summary: Jessica Daugirdas, a Brazilian influencer, died at 35 after a three-year fight with colorectal cancer. Her family confirmed her death on Instagram on January 25. Known for sharing her health journey online, Jessica inspired thousands with her honesty, strength, and faith while facing cancer and its many challenges.

stories.title: Use gender-neutral terms, courts told
stories.summary: Delhi High Court has adopted gender-neutral terminology in court documents, replacing father's/husband's name with parent's/spouse's name. This change, inspired by a district judge's suggestion, aims to empower women and reflect modern family structures. The move will impact judicial officers' personal files, staff ID cards, and various official forms.

stories.title: Fire at Kolkata warehouse: 7 dead, 21 missing
stories.summary: A devastating fire engulfed a Kolkata warehouse complex early Monday, claiming at least seven lives and leaving 21 workers missing. Trapped inside units laden with combustible decoration materials and food supplies, the victims were sleeping when the blaze erupted. Firefighters battled for hours, but the inferno's intensity and smoldering debris continue to hinder rescue efforts.

stories.title: Alert: UK households urged to stockpile three essentials ahead of Storm Chandra power cut risk
stories.summary: Storm Chandra is set to bring disruptive weather across the UK from late Monday into Tuesday, with heavy rain, strong winds and snow triggering multiple Met Office warnings. Flooding is likely in parts of southern England, while northern England and Scotland face hill snow and travel disruption. Households are urged to prepare for possible power cuts.

stories.title: West Virginia woman arrested in alleged Trump assassination plot; sheriff says she recruit people on social media
stories.summary: A West Virginia woman, Morgan Morrow, faces charges for allegedly attempting to recruit individuals to assassinate President Donald Trump. Authorities apprehended Morrow after discovering a TikTok post where she seemingly solicited a sniper. She reportedly admitted to posting the message, citing personal reasons for her animosity towards the President.

stories.title: ‘Stay away from USA’: Former FIFA chief Sepp Blatter fuels World Cup 2026 boycott debate
stories.summary: Amidst rising geopolitical tensions and concerns over US policies, a growing chorus is calling for a boycott of the 2026 FIFA World Cup co-hosted by the United States. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has publicly supported calls for fans to stay away, citing recent incidents and the perceived contradiction with the tournament's spirit of unity.

stories.title: YouTuber WhistlinDiesel faces another tax arrest after previous 2025 case
stories.summary: Popular YouTuber WhistlinDiesel, Cody Detwiler, was arrested again for a $30,000 tax dispute, claiming he received no prior notice. This follows a previous tax evasion arrest in November 2025. Detwiler stated the issue stems from a vehicle registered in Montana that was later destroyed, leading to a prolonged tax case without official notification.

stories.title: 'Maybe Vance wants to signal...': Former Indian diplomat on why JD Vance has been blocking US-India deal
'Attacking H1-B was the best thing...': Canadian-Indian entrepreneur on big tech layoffs in US
MrBeast criticizes Netflix pay, would give Alex Honnold over $500K for Taipei 101 stunt
stories.summary: Daredevil Alex Honnold's breathtaking free solo of Taipei 101 has sparked a bidding war, with YouTuber MrBeast claiming he'd have paid over $500,000 for the stunt on his platform. Honnold's 90-minute climb, broadcast live on Netflix, highlights the growing appeal of extreme urban feats and the fierce competition between streaming giants for high-stakes entertainment.

stories.title: In Republic Day messages, Trump hails historic bond, Xi talks of dragon-elephant tango
stories.summary: Global leaders, including US President Trump and China's Xi Jinping, extended Republic Day greetings to India. Trump emphasized the bond between the world's oldest and largest democracies, while Xi highlighted India-China as "good neighbours, friends and partners." King Charles III also lauded the enduring India-UK partnership, noting shared values and deepening cooperation.

stories.title: 'H-1B is something I have no control of': Indian-origin Frisco councilman Burt Thakur on why he has Indian donors
Bangor plane crash kills 7: Private jet linked to ‘anti‑Trump’ lawyers who defended illegal aliens
Did Tim Walz ask Donald Trump to work together? Minnesota governor, US president have ‘productive’ call over ICE protests
stories.summary: Following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti by a Border Patrol agent, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and President Trump held a "productive" call. Trump agreed to allow the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to investigate the incident and to review reducing federal agent numbers in the state.

stories.title: India, EU finalise FTA, deal set to be announced today
stories.summary: India and the European Union have finalized a comprehensive free trade agreement after 18 years of talks, poised to boost trade and investment. The deal, expected to be announced Tuesday, aims for significant tariff reductions on most goods, with India gaining market access for textiles and leather, while offering concessions on automobiles and wines. Implementation is anticipated by early 2027.

stories.title: Russia to hire 40,000 Indian workers in 2026, paying up to $1,000 amid labour shortage: Report
stories.summary: In a bold move to tackle its acute labor shortage, Russia is gearing up to welcome more than 40,000 Indian workers by 2026. This strategic decision comes in the wake of demographic challenges and an ongoing conflict, underlining the need for skilled labor. Following a recent mobility agreement, many Indian professionals are already contributing to the Russian workforce.

stories.title: Republic Day: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta lays foundation stone for slum development projects
stories.summary: "The previous governments spread fear that the BJP would stop free electricity and water, but these slum dwellers can now live peacefully. We are committed to providing them a good and quality life," Gupta told reporters.

stories.title: PIO civil servant gets flak on X for negotiating Chagos deal
stories.summary: A British civil servant of Indian origin, Dr. Francis Vijay Narasimhan Rangarajan, faces social media backlash over the controversial Chagos deal. He led negotiations to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius, retaining use of the Diego Garcia base. Critics, including former politicians, have voiced strong opposition to the agreement.

stories.title: 'Boring as hell': Trump reveals why he 'dozes off' during cabinet meeting; has nothing to do with health
'I can handle it': Mark Carney shrugs off Donald Trump’s ‘Governor’ jibe amid 100% tariff threat
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed Donald Trump's 'Governor' remark, stating he can handle it. Trump, threatening a 100% tariff, accused Canada of becoming a 'Drop Off Port' for Chinese goods. Carney, while not commenting on every tweet, emphasized the importance of respecting Canadian troops amidst the escalating trade tensions.

stories.title: British nationals charged with ‘targeting’ Pakistan dissidents in UK
stories.summary: Three British nationals have been charged with targeting two prominent Pakistani dissidents in the UK, supporters of jailed former PM Imran Khan. The men allegedly conspired to assault journalist Adil Raja and former Khan advisor Mirza Shahzad Akbar on December 24th. One suspect also faces charges for attempted arson at Akbar's home on New Year's Eve.

stories.title: Decline of Himalayan rivers could trigger nuclear war: UK report
stories.summary: UK intelligence warns of global food and water crises by the 2030s due to ecosystem collapse, potentially sparking conflict. Himalayan river decline could escalate tensions between China, India, and Pakistan, risking nuclear war. The report highlights threats to UK food security and calls for ecosystem protection and restoration.

stories.title: A century in uniform: Chandigarh girl carries 4 generations of Army service to Kartavya Path
Kashmir peaceful, ready to welcome visitors: Deputy CM
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary stated that Pakistan's efforts to disrupt tourism in the region have failed. He urged people to visit Kashmir, emphasizing its peaceful atmosphere and readiness to welcome visitors, while also honoring the victims of a past terror attack.

stories.title: From Bathinda to Kartavya Path: Punjab lad commands T-90 Bhishma tank at RD parade
Stage harassment allegation: Former TMC MP Mimi Chakraborty files police complaint
Kashmir braces for heavy snowfall after last week’s spell
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir is preparing for more heavy snowfall. A western disturbance is expected to bring snow starting Monday evening. This could affect flights and the Jammu-Srinagar highway. Moderate to heavy snowfall is forecast for most of Kashmir and higher Jammu regions on Tuesday. Light rain and higher-reach snow are possible Wednesday.

stories.title: ‘Insensitive and insulting’: BJP says Rahul Gandhi declined to wear Assamese Gamosa; Congress counters
stories.summary: The BJP has criticized Rahul Gandhi for allegedly not wearing an Assamese 'Gamosa' at a Republic Day reception, with Assam's CM demanding an apology. Congress countered by questioning why Defence Minister Rajnath Singh wasn't also asked to wear it, accusing the BJP of trivial politics and highlighting alleged disrespect towards their leaders at the parade.

stories.title: Have you ever paid your employer from salary? Immigration expert explains what this question by a border agent to an H-1B worker means
Train to Pahalgam faces backlash; NC, PDP ask railway minister to rethink
stories.summary: A proposed railway line from Bijbehara to Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir is facing strong opposition from local residents and political figures. Concerns are mounting over the project's impact on vast agricultural and apple orchard lands, threatening livelihoods. Leaders are urging the central government to reconsider the plan, citing existing infrastructure and the project's perceived lack of benefit.

stories.title: Could the UK bring back mandatory military service? What happens if you refuse
stories.summary: Amid rising global tensions and a shrinking British Army, the idea of conscription has resurfaced in public debate, though ministers insist there are no plans to reinstate it. Experts suggest modern refusal would likely incur fines rather than imprisonment, with exemptions for essential workers and conscientious objectors. Polls show significant reluctance among younger adults, highlighting challenges if conscription were ever enforced.

stories.title: Iran tensions: US aircraft carrier, warships arrive in Middle East
‘Hindu man looking down...’: Casey Putsch says Vivek Ramaswamy is working with ‘anti-Christ’
Stagger station revamp to prioritise funding of rail corridors, govt panel tells railways
stories.summary: An inter-ministerial panel has advised Indian Railways to stagger station redevelopment projects, prioritizing funding for programmatic corridors. The panel also recommended linking station development expenditure to revenue generation, including user charges, and suggested rolling out Integrated Station Facility Managers to maximize income from station assets.

stories.title: ‘Americans who hate Indians…’: Social media reacts to free samosas given at anti‑ICE protests
Private jet crashes in US: 7 killed, 1 severely injured; aircraft went down shortly after takeoff
‘No anaesthesia for MAGA’: Florida nurse refuses to treat Republicans, sparks calls for suspension
stories.summary: A Florida nurse named Erik Martindale has stirred up a storm on social media after declaring on Facebook that he would deny anesthesia to MAGA supporters. His bold statement has sparked outrage and prompted calls for the revocation of his nursing license. In a twist, Martindale later claimed his social media accounts had been compromised.

stories.title: Russian oil goes to India, Europeans buy refined products from them: Scott Bessent
Mass dog killings rattles Telangana: 200 more canines found dead in Hanamkonda; toll rises to 1,100
Agriculture scientists and innovative farmers get Padma Shri boost for their pioneering efforts
stories.summary: In a grand tribute to innovation in agriculture, nine distinguished individuals have been honored with the Padma Shri. Among them are esteemed scientists and passionate farmers, recognized for their impactful work ranging from the creation of superior rice strains and genome-editing breakthroughs to the promotion of unique cultivation methods such as Makhana farming.

stories.title: ‘No more hostages in Gaza’: IDF recovers last captive held by Hamas; remains repatriated to Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military has recovered the remains of Ran Gvili, the last hostage held in Gaza, confirming all abductees have been returned to Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu hailed this as an extraordinary achievement, fulfilling a promise to bring everyone back. Hamas stated the discovery confirms their commitment to the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: ‘Colonial mindset’: Padma Shri row over cow dung, urine remarks; Sridhar Vembu backs IIT Madras director
stories.summary: A political row erupted on social media after the Congress questioned IIT Madras director V Kamakoti's Padma Shri award, linking it to research on cow dung and urine. Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu strongly defended Kamakoti, highlighting his deep tech expertise and the scientific potential of traditional substances, criticizing a "slavish colonial mindset."

stories.title: Tough but fair: Why is Donald Trump sending Tom Homan to Minneapolis in a snub to Kristi Noem?
Who is Suella Braverman? British-Indian leader quits Conservatives and joins Reform UK
J&K: Army soldier injured in landmine blast near LoC in Rajouri
Kristi Noem called ‘sicko fan’ by DHS officials after Minnesota nurse killed by federal agents
Protocol vs politics: Congress questions Rahul's, Kharge's third-row seating at Republic Day parade; BJP hits back
‘Insult to Maharashtra’: Oppn slams Padma Bhushan for Koshiyari; ex-governor shrugs off criticism
stories.summary: Opposition leaders slammed the Centre's decision to award Padma Bhushan to former Maharashtra Governor Bhagat Singh Koshiyari, citing his alleged role in toppling the MVA government and insulting state icons. However, CM Devendra Fadnavis defended the award, highlighting Koshiyari's societal contributions and work for development.

stories.title: 'Self-sabotage': Indian-American entrepreneurs reject JD Vance as 'India's friend' after trade deal 'leaked' audio; 'To appease the groypers'
Mystery solved: What makes the sliding rocks of Death Valley move on their own
After a gap of over 10 years, India marks Republic Day in Yemen
stories.summary: For the first time in over a decade, India celebrated Republic Day in Yemen with the Indian community and embassy staff. Other diplomatic missions in the US, Singapore, Japan, and Sri Lanka also marked the occasion with flag unfurling ceremonies and participation from the Indian diaspora. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended greetings, highlighting the strong bilateral partnership.

stories.title: ChatGPT ‘nearly kills’ woman after giving confident advice about a poisonous plant
stories.summary: A YouTuber has warned of the dangers of trusting AI after ChatGPT repeatedly misidentified poison hemlock as harmless carrot foliage, nearly putting her friend at risk. Despite visual evidence, the chatbot doubled down with confident reassurances. The incident highlights how AI errors, especially in health and safety contexts, can have serious real-world consequences.

stories.title: Row over Tulsi Gabbard’s past link to Indian-American lawyer who said ‘kick Trump’
Evening news wrap: India flexes might on 77th Republic Day parade; UAE scraps Pakistan airport deal & more
stories.summary: India marked its 77th Republic Day with a grand parade showcasing military might and cultural diversity. Meanwhile, the UAE reportedly scrapped its airport management deal with Pakistan following the UAE President's India visit. In other news, a Bangladesh court sentenced three police officers to death for protest-related killings, and IndiGo cancelled flights to four Central Asian cities due to regional developments.

stories.title: Canada PM Mark Carney likely to visit India in March: Uranium, trade pact on agenda; comes days after China pivot
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is slated to visit India in early March to sign significant deals on uranium, energy, minerals, AI, education, and culture. This visit aims to diversify Canada's alliances and reset bilateral relations, with formal CEPA negotiations also set to commence. Both nations are prioritizing these agreements amid a changing global order and U.S. trade pressures.

stories.title: MrBeast steps into food tech spotlight after tasting cultivated chicken, drawing millions into future food debate
stories.summary: MrBeast brought cultivated meat into the mainstream after tasting cell-based chicken at Upside Foods’ California facility. His visit offered millions of young followers a rare look at how meat can be grown from cells without slaughter. The moment gave alternative protein a cultural boost, helping shift perception from niche food tech to something familiar and accessible.

stories.title: UAE influencers could face AED 10,000 fine for missing January 31 'Advertiser Permit' deadline
stories.summary: UAE content creators and advertisers must secure a mandatory Advertiser Permit by January 31, 2026, to avoid fines up to AED 10,000. This new regulation by the UAE Media Council aims to enhance transparency and professionalism in the digital advertising landscape.

stories.title: 'Dragon and elephant dance together': China's Xi greets President Droupadi Murmu on 77th Republic Day
“The only race of women who….”: Social media erupts as Clavicular’s comments about Black women trigger backlash
stories.summary: Clavicular is facing backlash after a viral clip showed him bluntly dismissing interest in Black women. The resurfaced comment sparked intense fan reaction, with social media users debating dating culture, racial fixation, and why such remarks continue to dominate online conversations. The clip quickly crossed millions of views, amplifying criticism and discourse.

stories.title: January 26, 1950: Revisiting India’s first Republic Day — the parade and those who watched history unfold
stories.summary: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day with a grand parade on Kartavya Path, showcasing military might and cultural diversity. The event marked the EU's first military parade participation outside Europe, reflecting India's growing global ties. The celebrations honored the nation's journey since becoming a sovereign democratic republic on January 26, 1950.

stories.title: One vote, unequal weight: Kothnur has just 10.9k elections, RR Nagar nearly 50k
stories.summary: Bengaluru's new municipal structure reveals significant voter disparities across wards, with some representing over 49,000 electors while others have just over 10,000. This imbalance undermines democratic representation and could lead to unequal access to civic services and political influence. The delimitation process, based on 2011 census population figures, has resulted in these inequities.

stories.title: Who is the owner of Greenland: Inside the story of the Viking murderer who named the land and built a lost Norse world
77th R-Day: Donald Trump extends greetings on Republic Day; hails India-US ties as a ‘historic bond’ of world’s largest democracies
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended heartfelt greetings to India on its 77th Republic Day, highlighting the "historic partnership" between the world's oldest and largest democracies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ambassador Sergio Gor also conveyed wishes, emphasizing strong cooperation across various sectors and the symbolic presence of US-made aircraft at the parade.

stories.title: Bangladesh crisis: Tribunal sentences 3 police officers to death; 5 others get jail terms
‘We all benefit’: EU chief says ‘successful India makes world more stable’, after attending Republic Day parade
stories.summary: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen stated that a successful India contributes to global stability, prosperity, and security. She, along with European Council president Antonio Costa, were the first joint EU leaders to attend India's Republic Day parade as chief guests. Their visit precedes an India-EU summit focused on trade, security, and strategic cooperation.

stories.title: THIS world’s largest underground city under Cappadocia kept 20,000 people alive without seeing daylight
Ramadan 2026: Expected dates, fasting hours, and seasonal shifts explained
stories.summary: Muslims worldwide anticipate a more moderate Ramadan in 2026, with fasting hours expected between 12-13 hours in Arab nations. This shift from recent summer fasts, due to the holy month falling in late winter/early spring, promises cooler temperatures and shorter daylight. Even in higher latitudes, fasting will be less demanding than previous years.

stories.title: Army’s 'phased battle array', IAF flypast and cultural diversity take centre stage — key takeaways from 77th Republic Day
stories.summary: India celebrates its 77th Republic Day on Monday, with nationwide events marking the adoption of the Constitution and highlighting the country’s cultural and military heritage. Celebrations of the 77th Republic Day at the Kartvya Path were based on the theme of the 150th Anniversary of the national song, Vande Mataram, a timeless mantra that awakened the spirit of Swadeshi, self-reliance, and freedom in India's national consciousness.

stories.title: Frozen America: A brutal winter storm has gripped the United States - in pics
stories.summary: A massive winter storm battered large parts of the United States, bringing heavy snow, sleet and freezing rain that disrupted travel, power supply and daily life. Millions were placed under winter weather warnings as Arctic cold followed the system, pushing temperatures to dangerous lows. Flight cancellations surged across major airports, while power outages left homes and businesses in the dark, especially in southern states unaccustomed to severe ice. Cities from New York and Washington to Chicago and Philadelphia struggled with icy roads and emergency closures. Authorities warned that extreme cold could prolong disruptions and pose life-threatening risks.

stories.title: This 3,000-year-old treasure in Spain was made with iron that fell from the sky
BrahMos to S-400: Weapon systems from Operation Sindoor take centre stage at Republic Day parade
stories.summary: India's Republic Day 2026 parade showcased its military might, highlighting the success of Operation Sindoor, a counterterror action that neutralized over 100 terrorists and enemy soldiers. The display featured advanced weapons platforms like the BrahMos missile and S-400 air defence system, emphasizing combat readiness and technological prowess in multi-domain warfare.

stories.title: World’s longest road tunnel takes drivers on a 20-minute journey without daylight beneath Norway’s mountains
Dubai’s Gulfood 2026: Two venues, 8,500 exhibitors and the world’s biggest food show
stories.summary: Gulfood 2026, the world's largest food trade show, has doubled its exhibition space across two Dubai venues for the first time in its 31-year history. This expansion accommodates over 8,500 exhibitors from 195 countries, showcasing 1.5 million products. The move aims to solidify Dubai's position as the global food trade headquarters, offering a more organized and expansive sourcing experience.

stories.title: Qatar Labour Ministry urges worker safety amid dusty, windy conditions in Doha
stories.summary: Doha faces dusty and windy weather. The Ministry of Labour has issued an advisory to employers. Companies must step up safety measures for outdoor workers. Protective equipment and adjusted schedules are crucial. This ensures worker wellbeing and safe work environments amidst adverse conditions. Continuous monitoring of weather is advised.

stories.title: 77th Republic Day: PM Modi dons maroon-yellow Rajasthani safa with zari motifs
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's red Rajasthani turban, adorned with golden-yellow streaks, captivated onlookers at the 77th Republic Day parade. This distinctive headwear, a recurring signature, symbolizes India's rich cultural tapestry and regional heritage. Paired with a navy kurta-pyjama and light blue Nehru jacket, his attire blended formal elegance with cultural pride, complementing the grandeur of the national celebration.

stories.title: Vikings reached America 1,000 years before Christopher Columbus; scientists confirm
Winter storm in US: Private jet carrying 8 passengers crashes during takeoff
stories.summary: A private Bombardier Challenger 600 jet crashed during takeoff at Bangor International Airport in Maine on Sunday night, carrying eight people. The incident occurred amid a severe winter storm battering the eastern United States, disrupting air travel nationwide. Federal authorities, including the FAA and NTSB, have launched an investigation into the cause of the crash.

stories.title: Dubai Culture signs deal with Spotify to bring more local music to UAE listeners
stories.summary: Dubai Culture and Spotify have inked a groundbreaking MoU to boost the region's music scene. This strategic alliance aims to empower local artists with resources, mentorship, and data insights, fostering sustainable careers and global reach. The initiative promises a richer, more diverse musical landscape for listeners, ensuring Dubai's creators gain international recognition and economic benefits.

stories.title: “Brothers Forever”: UAE announces week-long nationwide festival celebrating decades of ties with Kuwait
stories.summary: The UAE is launching a nationwide celebration, "UAE and Kuwait: Brothers Forever," from January 25 to February 4, to honor its deep-rooted relationship with Kuwait. The week-long event features over 40 social, cultural, and entertainment activities across all seven emirates, highlighting economic, educational, media, cultural, and sporting ties.

stories.title: UAE weather alert: Rain and hailstorm hit Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah as temperatures drop to 12°C
stories.summary: The UAE experienced a rare weather event as a low-pressure system brought hail and heavy rainfall to northern and eastern regions. Temperatures dropped significantly across the country, prompting advisories for motorists and residents to exercise caution due to reduced visibility and rough sea conditions. Fog is expected to develop in the coming mornings.

stories.title: Republic Day parade: India showcases military might, growth story — top developments
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi presided over the main ceremony at Kartavya Path in the national capital. The President of the European Council, Antonio Costa, and the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, also attended the celebrations as chief guests. Kartavya Path, which runs from Rashtrapati Bhavan to the National War Memorial, was extensively decorated to reflect India’s journey over the years.

stories.title: Mexico shooting: 11 killed in armed attack at soccer field in Guanajuato
stories.summary: At least 11 people were killed and 12 injured in a soccer field shooting in Salamanca, Guanajuato, on Sunday. Security forces are searching for the perpetrators. The incident occurred in a state already grappling with high homicide rates due to criminal group conflicts.

stories.title: UAE and Malaysia deepen anti-corruption cooperation through new agreement
stories.summary: The UAE Accountability Authority and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission have formalized closer coordination on accountability and integrity. This Memorandum of Understanding aims to enhance anti-corruption efforts through collaboration, shared expertise, and stronger governance practices, promoting transparency and integrity in both nations.

stories.title: 'We remain vigilant to developments around Iran': IndiGo cancels flights to four cities till Jan 28
stories.summary: IndiGo has cancelled flights to Tbilisi, Almaty, Tashkent, and Baku until January 28 due to regional developments around Iran. The airline cited a review of the security situation and emphasized passenger safety as its highest priority. This decision follows widespread unrest in Iran, with protests escalating against the country's leadership.

stories.title: 'Cooperate, turn over all illegal aliens': Trump's targets governor Walz amid immigration crackdown
stories.summary: Donald Trump urged all Democratic governors and mayors to cooperate with his administration on immigration enforcement, blaming Joe Biden for a surge in illegal immigration and rising violence. He specifically called on Minnesota's Governor Walz and Minneapolis Mayor Frey to assist in deporting "criminal illegal aliens" and demanded an end to "sanctuary cities."

stories.title: India marks 77th republic day: Who are this year’s chief guests?
stories.summary: India celebrates its 77th Republic Day with a grand parade on Kartavya Path, showcasing military might and cultural diversity. European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president António Costa are this years chief guests, highlighting a deepening strategic partnership. Discussions on a crucial free trade agreement and a new security pact are underway, underscoring strong India-EU ties.

stories.title: Ferry carrying 350 passengers sinks off southern Philippines, at least 15 dead
stories.summary: A ferry carrying over 350 people sank off the southern Philippines, resulting in at least 15 fatalities. Over 300 individuals were rescued following a distress call from a coast guard officer on board. Investigations are underway to determine the cause of the sinking, which occurred in good weather conditions.

stories.title: ‘No intention’: Canada's Carney rules out free trade pact with China after Trump threatens tariffs
stories.summary: Canada's prime minister Mark Carney denies plans for a free trade deal with China. This comes after US President Donald Trump threatened tariffs on Canadian goods. Carney affirmed Canada's commitment to the CUSMA agreement, which restricts such deals with non-market economies without prior notice. Carney said recent engagements with China focused on resolving existing tariff disputes, not broader trade pacts.

stories.title: Archaeologists uncover 800,000-year-old human footprints beneath the sands of eastern England
Minnesota Guard hands out coffee to anti-ICE protesters after deadly federal shooting
stories.summary: Minnesota National Guard troops were seen distributing coffee and hot chocolate to anti-ICE protesters amid heightened tensions following a fatal shooting. Wearing reflective vests to avoid confusion with federal agents, their presence aimed to manage crowds and de-escalate the volatile situation, creating a striking contrast that fueled online debate.

stories.title: How ink, art and India came together in the Constitution
